2027: PDP’ll reclaim Kaduna, Bawa declares
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Kaduna State, Shehu Usman Bawa, popularly known as ABG, has expressed confidence that the party will return to power in the state in the 2027 governorship election. Bawa also promised to adopt a different approach to tackling insecurity, infrastructure deficit and other development challenges confronting the state if elected governor. The PDP candidate spoke at the weekend, while interacting with journalists at his campaign office in Kaduna, where he outlined his plans for the state and discussed the party’s preparations for the 2027 election. He said the PDP was engaging stakeholders and communities across the state to explain its position and seek support for a change of government. “We were actually going out to enlighten the public on why they need to vote this government out,” Bawa said. He criticised what he described as the failure of the present administration to sufficiently prioritise development projects according to the needs of individual communities. Bawa said public resources should be channelled towards projects that directly addressed the priorities identified by residents. “These are public funds. All these monies do not belong to anybody. If you have projects that are a priority for a particular constituency, we should do the needful,” he said. He said his administration, if elected, would adopt a “bottom-to-top approach” to development by consulting communities before determining the projects to be executed. According to him, government should not embark on projects without first determining whether they reflect the immediate needs of the people. “As a governor, you can decide to do 10 kilometres of road in a particular constituency while that is not what they need. “It is possible the constituency doesn’t even have potable water; they don’t have medical centres; they don’t have so many things. But when you interface with them, you give them what they need,” he said. On insecurity, Bawa said his administration would pursue a different strategy, with the objective of creating an environment where residents could farm, travel and conduct their businesses without fear of kidnapping or attacks. “We want a Kaduna that all of us here can go to our farms, can go to the market without any fear. “You can go and harvest what you farm without any fear of being kidnapped,” he said. The PDP candidate said the state needed a security strategy that would go beyond responding to attacks after they had occurred. “You don’t have to wait for them to attack for you to protect them. You go for them. You follow them right where they are,” he said. Asked whether his administration would combine kinetic and non-kinetic measures in addressing insecurity, Bawa said his campaign had already engaged security experts to develop strategies. “We’ll approach it differently, and I’m assuring you that we have a solution to that. “We already have consultants that are working for us on how to tackle this security issue,” he said. Reacting to claims by the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) that there was no strong opposition in Kaduna State, Bawa said the argument would be tested during the election. “If there’s no opposition, why are they worried?” he asked. He added, “By February, by God’s grace, everybody will find out if they have an opposition or not.” Bawa also alleged that opposition parties had encountered difficulties in securing spaces for campaign billboards in some parts of the state. He claimed that some billboard operators asked prospective clients about their political affiliation before accepting advertisements. “We actually paid to put our billboards. We called some of the numbers, and the billboard people would ask you, ‘Which party are you?’ If you are not in APC, they won’t put your billboard,” he alleged. He, however, said the PDP would not rely solely on rallies and billboards in its campaign, stressing that direct engagement with voters remained central to its strategy. “It is not by rally or by putting billboards that will give you victory,” Bawa said. On the PDP’s performance in the 2023 elections and the subsequent movement of some elected politicians away from the party, the governorship candidate maintained that the party’s grassroots structure remained intact. “The structure they used is a PDP structure. That structure still remains the way it is,” he said. According to him, many of the supporters who backed PDP candidates in the 2023 elections remained with the party despite subsequent political developments. “The same people that voted for them, those supporters that have actually been following day and night, they are still there in PDP,” he said. Bawa said the party would rely on its existing structure as it mobilises for the 2027 election. “We have our party. The structure is still intact, and that is the same structure we’re using for 2027. We believe in 2027 we’ll get more votes,” he said. He further said the PDP was presenting its manifesto as a basis for accountability if elected, adding that candidates at different levels of the party would be expected to take responsibility for their campaign promises. “All parties should have a manifesto, and if you go by your manifesto, you shouldn’t shift the goalposts. “I believe what PDP is bringing on board, from the State Assembly, House of Representatives, Senate and the governorship is that we are taking full responsibility for all our promises,” Bawa said. He said the campaign would continue with engagements across Kaduna State as the PDP mobilises supporters ahead of the 2027 governorship election. items.title: New Opobo ltraditional ruler unveils plan to make kingdom agric hub
items.description: The new paramount ruler of Opobo Kingdom, Rivers, Charles Jaja, says he will seek partnerships to make the kingdom a hub for agriculture and agribusiness in the Niger Delta. Jaja made this known during his coronation ceremony on Saturday in Opobo Town, Opobo/Nkoro Local Government Area of Rivers. He expressed optimism that accelerating agriculture development would create thousands of jobs and fast-track the development of the kingdom. According to him, Opobo was once known for its vibrant agro economy in the late 1800s, which transformed the old Eastern Niger Delta. He said that his forefather, King Jaja, built the kingdom’s economic influence through ingenuity and intelligence, particularly by dominating the waterways in his early days. Jaja pledged that his administration would strengthen economic ties across regions and explore partnerships capable of boosting agriculture and agribusiness. The traditional ruler also called for improved infrastructure in oil-bearing communities and optimal implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act. “We remain hopeful that the optimal implementation of the PIA will benefit oil-bearing communities,” he said. Jaja said that the needs Opobo people included durable roads, jetties, shoreline protection, quality healthcare, tertiary educational institutions and functional skills development centres. He commended the government for recognising the traditional institutions and pledged to promote unity, truth and Justice throughout the kingdom. Former President Goodluck Jonathan congratulated Jaja on his ascension to the throne, describing the coronation as a symbol of cultural preservation. Jonathan said that the Opobo throne represented the legacy of a proud people whose contributions to the development of the Niger Delta and Nigeria remained significant. He expressed confidence that Jaja’s reign would bring peace, unity and development to Opobo kingdom. “I am hopeful that you would enjoy the partnership that you deserve from the government and relevant authorities. “I am also confident that you will use the dignity of your office to preserve the values and traditions handed down by your forebears,” Jonathan said. Rivers Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, congratulated Jaja, saying that his coronation will further strengthen peace, unity and development in the kingdom. Represented the Deputy Governor, Prof. Ngozi Odu, Fubara described the coronation as a celebration of historical identity, culture and enduring heritage. He said that the rich tradition of the Opobo people remained an important part of the cultural identity of Rivers and Nigeria. “As a government, we recognise the important role of the traditional institution in preserving our cultural values and promoting unity within our communities. “We encourage our traditional rulers to continue to serve as custodians of our heritage, and partners in the development of our state,” he said. Fubara prayed that the traditional ruler’s reign would be marked by unity, progress and purposeful leadership. Prominent traditional rulers attended the coronation, including the Igwe of Onitsha, and the Olu of Warri. items.title: Nor’easter brings flooding as New York and New Jersey declare emergency
items.description: Tens of millions of people across the north-eastern US are in the path of a powerful storm bringing coastal flooding, power cuts, travel chaos and cancelled stadium events. The so-called nor’easter is bringing “dangerous coastal flooding and beach conditions, strong winds and heavy rainfall” to areas including New York City and Boston on Saturday, the US National Weather Service (NWS) said. States of emergency have been declared in New York and New Jersey, both of which faced a coastal deluge in some areas. Rain and strong winds are forecast from Virginia to Maine. In Brooklyn, a man was killed by a falling tree, the BBC’s US partner CBS News reported. The nor’easter has caused widespread power cuts. More than 100,000 households, nearly all in the northeast US, have lost electricity, according to tracker PowerOutage. The Federal Aviation Administration recommended air passengers check with airlines about their flight status. More than 2,400 flights have been delayed and another 1,199 grounded, according to FlightAware. Saturday’s full moon is projected to worsen coastal flooding. Streets and homes were inundated with floodwater in the coastal New Jersey communities of Surf City and Manasquan on Saturday. “I urge all New Jerseyans to take this storm seriously, stay alert and follow local guidance,” Governor Mikie Sherrill said. NWS said in its alert: “Prepare immediately for significant inundation in low-lying areas near the shore, including roads underwater and impacts to homes and businesses.” In New York, officials are warning of wind gusts of up to 55mph (86km/h) throughout the weekend, leading to downed trees and power lines. “Don’t travel if you don’t have to,” NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani told residents in a video message. “Do not drive or walk through floodwater.” In the Boston area, the Red Sox moved the last game in their series against the Chicago Cubs to Sunday afternoon in Florida. A professional football match between Red Bull New York and St Louis City SC was also cancelled. The Global Citizen Festival concert in New York City’s Central Park, which was to be headlined by Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and John Legend, will not go ahead. Ed Sheeran’s Boston concert was also among events called off due to the weather. Sheeran’s concert at the Gillette Stadium in the Boston area was cancelled for safety reasons, the venue said.

items.title: MC Oluomo leads tributes as Lagos NURTW leader, Baba Alado dies at 83
items.description: The National President of the National Union of Road Transport Workers, NURTW, Alhaji Musiliu Ayinde Akinsanya, popularly known as MC Oluomo, has led tributes following the death of Lagos grassroots leader, Chief Taoreed Faronbi, fondly known as Baba Alado. Faronbi died in the early hours of Saturday, September 26, 2026, at the age of 83. His death was confirmed by his family, with burial rites conducted shortly afterward in accordance with Islamic tradition. MC Oluomo, in a condolence message, mourned Faronbi, describing him as a respected figure whose contributions to the NURTW and the wider community would remain part of his legacy. Faronbi was a prominent figure within the Lagos transport union and was widely known for his longstanding involvement in the activities of the NURTW. Beyond the transport sector, he combined traditional, commercial and political influence across parts of Lagos. He was the Olori Ebi of the Alagbeji Royal Family in Papa Ajao, Mushin, and also held the chieftaincy title of Akinrogun of Isolo Kingdom. In the commercial sector, Faronbi was known as the Babaloja of Aswani International Market, a position that placed him at the centre of trading activities in the area for several years. His burial attracted relatives, friends, community members and prominent figures from across Lagos. Among those who attended were Senator Ganiyu Olanrewaju Solomon, the Executive Chairman of Mushin Local Government, Tunbosun Aruwe, and the Chairman of Odi-Olowo/Ojuwoye Local Council Development Area, Dr Oluseyi Jakande. Faronbi was also a familiar face in Lagos’ social and entertainment circles, maintaining relationships with leading Fuji and juju musicians. Among the artistes associated with him were K1 De Ultimate, Osupa Saheed and Alabi Pasuma. He was also involved in real estate and land development, although aspects of his activities in the sector occasionally generated disputes with communities and other parties. His death has since triggered tributes from politicians, transport union leaders, entertainers, traders and residents of Mushin, who have continued to mourn the loss of a figure who occupied several spheres of Lagos’ grassroots life. items.title: Polling underway in NA-168 Bahawalpur by-election
items.description: BAHAWALPUR: Polling was underway on Sunday in the NA-168 Bahawalpur by-poll, with a close contest expected between PML-N’s Malik Munir Iqbal Channar and independent candidate Wali Dad Cheema. The constituency fell vacant after the death of Malik Muhammad Iqbal Channar in August, whose son is now the ruling party’s candidate. Polling began at 8am and is expected to conclude at 5pm. Spokesperson for the Election Commission of Pakistan, Huda Gohar, told Dawn that voters present within the boundaries of the polling station will be allowed to cast their vote past 5pm as well. The polling process remained largely peaceful across the constituency. However, balloting was briefly disrupted at a polling station in Akhtarabad after a brawl between voters, a statement by the provincial election commissioner said. The incident involved alleged harassment of election staff by political workers, the statement said. The Provincial Election Commissioner Control Room took immediate action, while the relevant district returning officer (DRO) and returning officer (RO) brought the situation under control with the help of police. “The issue has since been resolved and polling is continuing as usual,” the statement added. According to data from the provincial election commissioner’s office, a total of 483,143 people are registered in the constituency, including 248,259 men and 234,614 women across 292 polling stations. At the polling stations, 307 presiding officers and 941 polling officers and assistant presiding officers have been deployed. A day earlier, the Punjab Home Department requested the federal interior ministry that troops of army and Rangers (Punjab) be deployed in the constituency for smooth, peaceful and secure conduct of the by-election. Leading up to the by-poll, three persons were injured on Sept 12 in an armed clash at Baqirpur in connection with the election campaign of Cheema, the son of former PML-Q federal minister Tariq Bashir Cheema. As per Rescue 1122 sources, the clash occurred during Cheema’s election rally between the supporters of the rival candidates, and some of them resorted to firing, resulting in injuries to three people.

items.title: Deputy chair of Turkey's AK Party resigns after trading allegation amid funds crisis
items.description: ANKARA, Sept 27 (Reuters) - A deputy chair of President Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AK Party stepped down after an opposition politician accused her of making a large profit on shares just before a funds crisis triggered a major selloff on the country's stock market. Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya, the AK Party's deputy chair responsible for social policies and who also served as family minister from 2016 to 2018, said late on Saturday she had asked Erdogan to relieve her of all her duties so the allegations could be investigated.

items.title: Acampada en Sol contra los desahucios, en directo | Sánchez confirma que el Gobierno está trabajando “a contra reloj” para aprobar el decreto de vivienda el martes
items.description: El jefe del Ejecutivo, Pedro Sánchez, ha confirmado este domingo en un mitin del PSOE en Getafe (Madrid) que el Gobierno “está trabajando a contra reloj” para aprobar el decreto de vivienda en el Consejo de Ministros del martes. El presidente se ha dirigido de forma directa a Maricarmen Abascal, desahuciada a sus 87 años esta semana del piso donde vivía. “Maricarmen, tengo un mensaje para ti: el Gobierno está trabajando contra reloj para llevar al martes el decreto ley de vivienda. Pido a los grupos parlamentarios que hagamos un último esfuerzo para que sea convalidado. No es una cuestión de ideología, es una cuestión de humanidad”, ha aseverado Sánchez. Los ministros de Sumar y varios dirigentes de la coalición han intensificado este fin de semana su presión al socio de Gobierno para que apruebe el próximo martes un decreto de vivienda ambicioso. La titular de Sanidad, Mónica García, ha defendido que el paquete de medidas incluya la prórroga de los alquileres hasta julio de 2028, la expropiación de algunas viviendas a fondos buitre, la prohibición de los desahucios a familias vulnerables o la regulación de los alquileres de temporada y habitaciones. Los manifestantes tienen intención de permanecer acampados al menos hasta el martes. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Europe-bound newlywed arrested with 72 wraps of cocaine in stomach at Enugu airport
items.description: A 25-year-old newlywed businessman, Lovely Chukwulobelu, has been arrested by operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) for allegedly attempting to traffic cocaine to Portugal. Chukwulobelu, in a statement signed by Femi Babafemi, NDLEA Director of Media and Advocacy on Sunday, was intercepted at the departure hall of Akanu Ibiam International Airport (AIIA), Enugu, on Thursday, September 25, 2026, while attempting to board an Ethiopian Airlines flight to Portugal via Addis Ababa. According to the NDLEA, the suspect had ingested 72 wraps of cocaine and was placed under excretion observation after his arrest. He subsequently excreted all 72 wraps of the Class A illicit drug. The agency said the suspect was wearing his wedding ring when he was arrested. Chukwulobelu reportedly told investigators that he previously operated a car decoration business at the Trade Fair Complex in the Ojo area of Lagos before relocating to Portugal in May 2023. He had recently returned to Nigeria and got married on September 13, 2026. The suspect allegedly said he turned to drug trafficking in an attempt to offset expenses incurred during his wedding. NDLEA intercepts 2.55 million opioid pills In another major operation, NDLEA operatives at the import shed of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Lagos, seized 2,550,000 pills of opioids during a joint examination of three monitored consignments. The agency said the consignments contained Tramaking 225mg, Tramaking 250mg and Royal Tapentadol 250mg, with a combined gross weight of 1,640.55kg. The consignments were imported from India and Bangladesh through Qatar Airways, RwandAir and Ethiopian Airlines. 262kg cannabis seized in Bauchi In Bauchi State, NDLEA officers arrested two suspects, Umar Hamidu, 35, and Abdulkarim Salihu, 45, along the Maiduguri bypass. The agency said the suspects were found with 300 compressed blocks of skunk, a strain of cannabis weighing 262.5kg. The drugs were allegedly concealed in the false bottom of a truck marked MUB757 YH. Meanwhile, NDLEA officers, supported by soldiers, destroyed two cannabis farms at Eko Camp, Ilushi, Edo State, estimated to have a combined yield of 1,360.23kg. NDLEA raids Lagos drug hotspots In Lagos, two women, Odumabo Kehinde, 36, and Obiekwe Chioma, 40, were arrested on Saturday, September 26, during a raid on Anifowoshe Street, Mushin. The operatives recovered 3.4kg of skunk from the suspects. In a separate operation at Ebute-Ero motor park on the same day, NDLEA officers arrested 58-year-old Ugwu Johnson and recovered several illicit consignments. The exhibits included 5.920kg of skunk, 2,400 ampoules of pentazocine injection, 8,400 tablets of nitrazepam and 40,000 pills of tramadol. Two Togolese arrested with 305kg cannabis Two Togolese nationals, Yinusa Abdulsamad, 35, and Fatai Baba, 33, were also arrested along the Iganna-Ilero road in Iganna, Oyo State. NDLEA said the suspects were intercepted with 305.6kg of skunk concealed in two pickup vans allegedly being used for cross-border trafficking. The agency said the cannabis was sourced from Ghana and being moved into Nigeria through the Oyo axis. At the Seme border in Badagry, Lagos, five suspects were arrested with 420 cartons of nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas. The substance weighed 1,688.4kg, while two vehicles allegedly used to transport the consignment from the border into Lagos were also seized. The suspects were identified as Kingsley John, 40; John Chibuike Okeke, 44; Lamidi Ismaila, 40; Babatunde Samuel, 42; and Afeesu Idowu, 47. Beyond its enforcement operations, the NDLEA said its commands and formations across the country continued their War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) sensitisation campaigns during the week. The campaigns were held at schools, worship centres, workplaces and communities, including Community High School, Saki, Oyo State; Auchi College, Auchi, Edo State; Alkali Modibbo Islamic Centre, Dukku, Gombe State; and Junior Arabic Secondary School, Kahu, Kibiya LGA, Kano State. The Delta Ports Command also paid a WADA advocacy visit to His Royal Majesty, Ogiame Atuwatshe III, the Olu of Warri, in Delta State. NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (rtd), commended officers and personnel of the MMIA, AIIA, Lagos, Oyo, Edo, Seme and Bauchi commands for the operations. Marwa urged officers across the country to sustain what he described as the agency’s balanced approach to drug control efforts. items.title: Le Maroc sacré champion d’Afrique et du monde de billard 2026
items.description: La sélection nationale marocaine de billard a remporté samedi soir à Marrakech, le titre de championne d’Afrique et du monde de la discipline. Au niveau du Championnat du monde de billard 2026, l'équipe nationale a battu en finale la sélection d’Irlande du Nord, sur le score de 11 à 9. La finale de l’épreuve par équipes a été particulièrement disputée entre les deux sélections, qui se sont livrées à un duel serré avant que l’équipe nationale ne s’impose, décrochant ainsi son deuxième titre mondial après celui remporté en 2014. La sélection nationale marocaine de billard s'était qualifiée pour la finale du Championnat du monde de billard 2026, en s’imposant face à la sélection du Pays de Galles sur le score de 11 à 7. Dans une déclaration à la presse, l’entraîneur de la sélection nationale, Yasser El Amrani, a souligné que ce sacre est le fruit du travail accompli par les joueurs tout au long de la compétition, notamment face à de solides sélections. De son côté, le joueur de l’équipe nationale, Abderrahmane Cherfi, a relevé, dans une déclaration similaire, que les éléments nationaux ont fait preuve d’une grande concentration et d’un fort esprit de compétition lors des différentes rencontres, couronnant ainsi leur parcours par un titre mondial décroché à domicile. Organisés du 17 au 27 septembre courant, sous l’égide de l’Ultimate Pool Association (UPA) et de l’International Eightball Pool Federation (IEPF), les Championnats d’Afrique et du monde de billard 2026 ont réuni près de 300 joueurs représentant quelque 18 pays, qui se sont affrontés dans 24 catégories, comprenant notamment les épreuves par équipes, individuelles, en double ainsi que les catégories Masters. The post Le Maroc sacré champion d’Afrique et du monde de billard 2026 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Mouctar Diallo à propos de Sidya Touré : « même dans l’adversité, il gardait son calme »
items.description: Dans un hommage poignant, l’ancien ministre Mouctar Diallo, depuis les Etats-Unis, revient sur près de deux décennies de compagnonnage avec Sidya Touré. Il évoque notamment leur engagement commun, les épreuves traversées au sein des Forces Vives et le traumatisme du 28 septembre 2009, où les deux hommes ont été grièvement blessés. HOMMAGE À SIDYA TOURÉ La tragique disparition de Monsieur Sidya Touré, ancien Premier ministre et président de l’UFR, ce vendredi 25 septembre 2026 à Paris, me laisse le cœur meurtri. Je perds un compagnon de lutte. La Guinée perd un homme de valeurs qui l’a profondément aimée. Notre première rencontre remonte à 2003, dans le cadre de mon engagement citoyen. Nos liens se sont resserrés lorsque j’étais le premier responsable de la jeunesse de la société civile guinéenne au sein du CNOSCG, notamment pendant les mobilisations de 2006 et 2007. J’étais alors aux côtés, entre autres, de Ben Sékou Sylla, Naby Diakité et Thierno Aliou Diaouné, aujourd’hui disparus. Que leurs âmes reposent en paix. Lorsque nous avons fondé le parti NFD (Nouvelles Forces Démocratiques), notre relation est devenue une collaboration constante, nourrie de confiance et de franchise. Au sein des Forces Vives, du Collectif des Partis Politiques, de l’Opposition Républicaine et d’autres plateformes, nous avons partagé les espoirs, les risques et les blessures du combat pour une Guinée démocratique. La lutte pour une Guinée meilleure nous a réunis. Les épreuves nous ont liés pour toujours. Le massacre du 28 septembre 2009 reste la plus douloureuse de ces épreuves. De la tribune du stade jusque dans le véhicule de Toumba Diakité qui nous escortait, nous avons traversé l’horreur ensemble. Malmenés et gravement blessés, nous nous tenions les uns aux autres, avec l’ancien Premier ministre Lounceny Fall. La mort était tout près. Cette solidarité dans la terreur reste gravée en moi. Je garde aussi le souvenir des négociations d’Abuja 1 et 2 et de Ouagadougou 1 et 2, organisées par la CEDEAO et le président du Burkina Faso entre nous, représentants des Forces Vives, et le CNDD. Je me souviens de nos longues réunions et de nos conversations plus intimes, à la Minière, à Coléah, à Paris ou ailleurs, ainsi qu’au téléphone. Au cœur de nos échanges revenait toujours la même préoccupation : la Guinée, son avenir et ce que nous pouvions encore lui donner. Sidya Touré alliait compétence, expérience, vision et mesure. Même dans l’adversité, il gardait son calme. Il reconnaissait le talent, encourageait les compétences et savait transmettre. Grand serviteur de l’État, homme d’État accompli, entrepreneur à succès et dirigeant politique engagé, il a laissé une empreinte indélébile en Guinée comme en Côte d’Ivoire. Il avait tant donné. Il voulait encore servir. Puissions-nous honorer sa mémoire à la hauteur de son engagement. Puissions-nous surtout faire vivre ce qu’il nous laisse : l’exigence de compétence et de rigueur, la constance dans les convictions et l’amour du pays. À sa famille, à ses proches, à ses compagnons de l’UFR ainsi qu’aux peuples de Guinée et de Côte d’Ivoire, j’adresse mes condoléances les plus attristées. Qu’Allah, le Sage et le Juste, lui accorde Sa miséricorde, l’accueille au Firdaws et donne aux siens la force de traverser cette immense douleur. Dors en paix, cher Président ! items.title: Clôture SITHO 2026 : le Djôrô, région invitée d’honneur de la 17e édition
items.description: Le Ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert OUEDRAOGO, représentant le Camarade Premier Ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel OUÉDRAOGO, et accompagné de son collègue de la Santé, Robert Lucien Jean Claude KARGOUGOU, a présidé la cérémonie de clôture de la 16ᵉ édition du Salon International du Tourisme et de l’Hôtellerie de Ouagadougou (SITHO), dans la soirée du samedi 26 septembre 2026, sur l'esplanade du SIAO. Du 22 au 27 septembre 2026, le SITHO a déroulé son programme d'activités en offrant un cadre unique de valorisation du patrimoine culturel burkinabè et de promotion des richesses touristiques des pays invités spéciaux, le Mali et le Niger. Durant cette soirée, des pionniers du SITHO ont reçu des attestations de reconnaissance. Des prix spéciaux ont également été décernés à des acteurs de la gastronomie, de l'hôtellerie et à des agences de promotion touristique, pour leurs innovations. Concernant les prix officiels, l'excellence des acteurs du tourisme et de l'hôtellerie a été primée dans les catégories Hackathon solution tech, Pitch de projet touristique, Art culinaire et Meilleur stand. Dans son discours de clôture, le Ministre Pingdwendé Gilbert OUEDRAOGO a exprimé sa satisfaction quant au bon déroulement de l’événement, avec une mention spéciale faite aux membres du comité d'organisation. Durant ces jours d'activités intenses, la diversité des participants et la richesse des échanges ont permis de rapprocher les différents maillons de la chaîne touristique et de favoriser le dialogue entre les monteurs de projets et les structures de financement, à la lumière du thème >. En résumé, l'exposition professionnelle a regroupé 138 stands tandis que 277 participants ont pris part aux excursions touristiques grand public. Le chef du département en charge du tourisme a donné rendez-vous aux acteurs du tourisme pour la 17e édition en 2027, placé sous le thème : «Patrimoines, hospitalités et intégrations : le tourisme au service du développement des territoires », avec la région du Djôrô comme région invitée d'honneur. items.title: Crise du blé en mer Noire : l’Algérie est-elle à l’abri ?
items.description: Le monde entier surveille l’évolution de la situation au détroit d'Ormuz et ses répercussions sur le marché énergétique, tandis qu’une autre guerre, celle entre l’Ukraine et la Russie, fait peser une menace certaine sur la sécurité alimentaire mondiale par les perturbations qu’elle provoque en mer Noire, voie importante d’exportation de céréales. Gros importateur de blé tendre, l’Algérie est-elle à l'abri de cette crise ? Un tiers des expéditions mondiales d’hydrocarbures transitent par le détroit d’Ormuz et autant de cargaisons céréalières passent par la mer Noire, en provenance de Russie et d’Ukraine, les deux principaux producteurs et exportateurs mondiaux de blé. L’escalade entre les deux pays et les attaques contre leurs ports respectifs, les terminaux céréaliers, les silos et les navires, ont nettement réduit les expéditions de navires céréaliers à partir de la mer Noire. Des voies alternatives insuffisantes et coûteuses Les approvisionnements sont perturbés depuis juillet dernier. Les voies intermédiaires, par route ou par train, sont non seulement insuffisantes, mais aussi coûteuses. La conjugaison de la hausse des cours énergétiques avec celle des prix des céréales risque de donner lieu à une inflation record, mettent en garde les économistes. Le plus dur est à venir, car pour le moment, “les risques liés à l’approvisionnement alimentaire n’ont pas encore été pleinement pris en compte sur un marché qui se concentre davantage sur le coût des matières premières telles que l’énergie”, indiquent des investisseurs cités par le média Asharq Business . “Le monde sous-estime l’impact de ces attaques”, déclare au même média Caitlin Welch , experte en sécurité alimentaire au Centre d’études stratégiques et internationales, basé à Washington. “On peut considérer la mer Noire comme aussi importante pour le commerce mondial du blé que le détroit d’Ormuz l’est pour le commerce mondial du pétrole”, ajoute-t-elle. Les prix du blé risquent de flamber encore Les prix du blé tendre, dont l’Algérie a déjà importé plus de 4 millions de tonnes depuis le début de l’année, ont déjà atteint leur plus haut niveau depuis trois ans, entre 300 et 330 dollars la tonne selon les variétés et les provenances, et pourraient encore augmenter vu les prévisions à la baisse des expéditions russes et ukrainiennes. L'institut de recherche SovEcon, spécialisé dans les marchés agricoles de la mer Noire, estime que les exportations cumulées de blé de la Russie et de l'Ukraine devraient s'établir à environ la moitié de leur niveau de l'année dernière au cours de la campagne agricole s'étendant de juillet à septembre. Les gros importateurs mondiaux se tournent vers des marchés alternatifs, mais qui ne peuvent toutefois pas remplacer les quantités qui provenaient d’Ukraine et de Russie à cause notamment de la sécheresse aux États-Unis et des chaleurs de l’été dernier en Europe. Les longues distances influent aussi sur les coûts. Algérie : le Département américain de l’agriculture USDA revoit ses prévisions à la baisse Cette situation affecte les pays les plus vulnérables, ceux qui ont une forte consommation de céréales et qui dépendent fortement des approvisionnements extérieurs. C’est le cas notamment de l’Égypte, de l'Indonésie, du Bangladesh, de l’Algérie et de plusieurs pays arabes. L’Algérie a pris ses devants dès le début de l’année en multipliant les achats de blé sur les marchés mondiaux. Dans ses précisions pour la saison 2026-2027, le département US de l’agriculture a revu à la baisse les achats attendus de l’Algérie de 8,5 à 8,3 millions de tonnes à cause de la hausse de ses stocks. En plus de ses silos pleins, l'Algérie est aussi mise à l'abri d’un éventuel choc par plusieurs facteurs endogènes, comme les subventions généralisées, le système d’importation centralisé et la diversification des sources d’approvisionnement. La crise du blé de la mer Noire illustre combien les projets agricoles lancés par l'Algérie dans le Sahara sont importants et stratégiques pour la sécurité alimentaire du pays. L’article Crise du blé en mer Noire : l'Algérie est-elle à l'abri ? est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: La crise de l’eau pourrait coûter à la Tunisie 6,4 % du PIB d’ici 2050
items.description: La pénurie d’eau risque de devenir l’un des principaux freins structurels à la croissance tunisienne et, en l’absence de mesures adéquates, pourrait réduire le PIB du pays de 6,4 % d’ici 2050. C’est l'alerte lancée par la Banque mondiale (BM) dans son dernier rapport Tunisia Economic Monitor intitulé «Tunisia's Water Challenge: From Scarcity to Resilience» (Le défi de l’eau en Tunisie : de la pénurie à la résilience). Ce rapport identifie la sécurité hydrique comme un facteur de plus en plus déterminant pour la croissance, l’emploi et la compétitivité. Selon l’institution de Washington, la Tunisie ne dispose aujourd’hui que de 380 mètres cubes d’eau douce renouvelable par habitant et par an, un niveau nettement inférieur au seuil international de pénurie d’eau absolue, qui est de 500 mètres cubes. Le secteur agricole est particulièrement exposé ; il emploie environ 14 % de la population active nationale et jusqu’à la moitié des travailleurs dans les zones rurales. Sans mesures correctives, le stress climatique et le manque d’eau pourraient entraîner la perte d’au moins 30 % des emplois agricoles d’ici le milieu du siècle, avec des répercussions également sur l’agro-industrie, le tourisme et l’industrie. Le rapport s’inscrit dans un contexte économique toujours marqué par une croissance modérée. Après une hausse de 2,7 % en 2025 et de 2,4 % en rythme annuel au premier semestre de cette année, la BM prévoit une progression du PIB de 2,3 % en 2026 et une croissance moyenne de 2,1 % sur la période 2027-2028. Le taux de chômage a reculé à 14,9 % au deuxième trimestre, mais demeure à 21,6 % chez les femmes. Pour transformer le «Plan Eau 2050» tunisien en une réponse structurelle, la BM préconise des investissements de l’ordre de 900 millions de dollars par an jusqu’au milieu du siècle, assortis d’une réforme de la gouvernance du secteur, d’une réduction des pertes sur les réseaux, de la réutilisation des eaux usées traitées, de la numérisation et d’une meilleure gestion de l’irrigation. Le programme RESEau, soutenu par la BM elle-même, devrait générer, lors de sa première phase, environ 4 000 emplois permanents et 13 400 emplois temporaires. I. B. items.title: Swiss vote on what it means to be neutral
items.description: The Swiss voted on Sunday on a much-debated proposal to tighten their country’s cherished neutrality, with polls indicating most would reject the initiative championed by the hard-right and dubbed “pro-Russian” by opponents. Polling stations opened on Sunday morning for in-person voting on those and other topics as part of Switzerland’s direct democracy system, although most people vote in advance by post. The Swiss widely embrace their neutrality , but an initiative to enshrine a strict definition into the constitution has exposed deep disagreement over what that neutrality entails. Switzerland’s traditional position is one of armed neutrality, but Russia’s war in Ukraine reopened questions over its non-engagement in foreign conflicts. Concerned over Bern’s decision to back the European Union’s economic pressure on Russia, the pro-sovereignty Pro Switzerland organisation collected enough signatures to trigger a referendum under the country’s direct democracy system on better anchoring neutrality in its constitution. The proposal has been roundly rejected by nearly the entire political establishment, with opinion polls indicating most voters will do the same. Moscow, which has slammed Switzerland for joining the EU sanctions and accused Bern of abandoning its neutrality, has meanwhile praised the initiative — dubbed “pro-Russian” by some opponents. The proposal calls for the constitution to guarantee that Swiss neutrality is “armed and perpetual”. It would prevent Switzerland, whose neutrality dates back to 1516 and has been internationally recognised since 1815, from establishing closer ties with NATO and would rule out any military alliance except if the country were attacked. And it would prohibit imposing sanctions unless called for by the United Nations. ‘Perpetual armed neutrality’ All sides in the debate argue that they want to maintain Switzerland’s neutrality. Both the Swiss government and parliament have rejected the proposal, arguing it is too dogmatic and would limit the country’s room for manoeuvre at a time of soaring geopolitical tensions. “Neutrality has always been applied with a degree of flexibility,” Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis said during a recent televised debate. While Switzerland had no plans to lift a ban on selling arms to countries in conflict, including to Ukraine, he stressed that “neutrality does not mean indifference”. The country, he said, would “not look away when we see violations of the very international rules that allow us to live in peace”. Nearly all major political parties have also turned their nose up at the initiative, with the exception of the hard-right Swiss People’s Party (SVP), the country’s largest party. “Our goal is to foster peace, diplomacy and dialogue,” SVP vice president Celine Amaudruz said during a televised debate. “To achieve that, we must maintain credibility through perpetual armed neutrality,” she insisted. While initial opinion polls had indicated that the vote might be tight, the final two surveys suggested a clear majority of voters — well above 60 per cent — would reject the initiative. Polls also suggested voters would reject the other national initiative on Sunday’s ballot, put forward by a non-partisan citizens’ movement and calling for the country to raise its food self-sufficiency rate to 70pc, up from 42pc in 2024. The government has warned that the target would be difficult, if not impossible, to reach, while most major parties also reject it as unrealistic. Polling stations will close at 12:00pm (3:00pm PKT) at the latest.

items.title: Sowore returns to Nigeria, set for 2027 presidential campaign
items.description: Mr Omoyele Sowore, presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), has returned to Nigeria from the United States on Sunday to resume his 2027 presidential campaign. Sowore disclosed this in a statement issued to newsmen on Sunday. He expressed excitement about returning to his family and country after more than 20 months away. According to him, he left for the U S. over what he described as arrests, detention, travel restrictions and the seizure of his international passport by Nigerian security agencies. Sowore said that while in the United States, he engaged Nigerians in the diaspora, supporters, activists and other stakeholders on the state of the country and his political agenda. He also said he participated in a solidarity march for Palestine in New York and continued his advocacy for voting rights for Nigerians living abroad. The AAC presidential candidate said he remained committed to Nigerians in the diaspora participating in the country’s democratic process. He said an AAC administration would pursue diaspora voting if elected president in 2027. Sowore said he was expected to arrive at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, before proceeding to Abuja. He said he would also continue to attend court proceedings in connection with the cybercrime case the Department of State Services (DSS) instituted against himin 2025. The candidate said his return would mark another phase of his nationwide campaign ahead of the 2027 presidential election. “I plan to engage workers, students, youths, women, farmers, traders, professionals and communities across the country, ” he said. He said the engagements would focus on the political, social and economic issues contained in the AAC’s 2027 agenda. He said that the campaign would seek to mobilise Nigerians around issues including equal rights, justice, peace, security and economic development. Sowore said the 2027 election would give Nigerians a chance to decide the direction of the country’s political leadership. “My campaign will continue to advocate fundamental political, social and economic transformation, ” he said. The AAC candidate said he remained committed to taking his message directly to Nigerians across the country. “I will continue the campaign and engagements with Nigerians as the 2027 election approaches, “he said. items.title: 4 reasons Super Eagles must beat Guinea-Bissau in AFCON 2027 qualifier
items.description: The Super Eagles will face Guinea-Bissau in their second Group L fixture of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON qualifiers on Tuesday, with the encounter carrying significant importance for Nigeria’s hopes of reaching the tournament. Nigeria opened their campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over Madagascar in Uyo, while Guinea-Bissau defeated Tanzania 2-0 to move top of the group on goal difference. With both teams on three points, the meeting provides Nigeria with an opportunity to move ahead of one of their main rivals. Here are four reasons why victory could be particularly important for the Super Eagles. 1. Only one qualification spot is available Group L presents a different qualification scenario because Tanzania are among the hosts of the 2027 AFCON alongside Kenya and Uganda and therefore have an automatic place at the tournament. That leaves Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar competing for the group’s available qualification spot. As a result, every point gained against a direct rival could prove important when the final standings are decided. 2. Guinea-Bissau currently lead the group Guinea-Bissau made a strong start by defeating Tanzania 2-0 in their opening fixture. Nigeria, meanwhile, had to come from behind to beat Madagascar 2-1. Both sides therefore have three points, but Guinea-Bissau sit above the Super Eagles on goal difference. A victory for Nigeria would allow Eric Chelle’s side to move ahead of the Djurtus after just two matches. 3. Nigeria can move to six points A win would take the Super Eagles to six points from their opening two games. That would give Nigeria an early advantage in the group and put pressure on the other teams chasing the available qualification position. After collecting maximum points against Madagascar, another victory would also give the Super Eagles the opportunity to establish momentum at the start of the campaign. 4. Nigeria can deny a direct rival points Perhaps the biggest significance of the fixture is that Guinea-Bissau are competing for the same qualification spot as Nigeria. A victory would therefore have a double effect for the Super Eagles: Nigeria would collect three points while Guinea-Bissau would leave the encounter without any. By contrast, a defeat would move the Djurtus three points clear of Nigeria, while a draw would keep both sides level on points. With only one competitive qualification place available in the group, the result could therefore have a significant bearing on the race as the AFCON campaign progresses Vanguard News The post 4 reasons Super Eagles must beat Guinea-Bissau in AFCON 2027 qualifier appeared first on Vanguard News .

Les USA financent un centre militaire naval tunisien à Bizerte
items.description: Les États-Unis ont attribué à la société turque Biltek Uluslararasi Insaat Limited Sirketi un contrat de 998 000 dollars pour la troisième phase du Maritime Center of Excellence (MCOE), actuellement en construction sur la base navale tunisienne de Bizerte. Selon l’ agence Ansa , l’attribution du marché a été publiée le 22 septembre sur SAM.gov par le Department of the Navy, par l'intermédiaire du Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Europe Africa Central (Navfac Euracent). L’Award Notice ou avis d’attribution, relatif au contrat N33191-26-C-0010, précise que Biltek a remporté le marché à l’issue d’une procédure concurrentielle à prix fixe. La phase III prévoit une tour d’entraînement à la descente en rappel et aux opérations en hauteur, ainsi qu’une zone d’atterrissage pour hélicoptères. L’appel d’offres inclut également, en option, une installation pour véhicules et embarcations ainsi qu’une rampe de mise à l’eau avec ponton. Ce centre est destiné à l’entraînement des commandos et des forces spéciales navales tunisiennes et s’inscrit dans le cadre des programmes américains de renforcement des capacités des partenaires (Building Partner Capacity). Washington et Tunis visent également à en faire un pôle régional pour des activités et des exercices multinationaux. Biltek avait déjà été chargée, en 2024, de réaliser une première tranche du complexe, comprenant une zone d’entraînement au combat rapproché, des champs de tir, un parcours d’obstacles et des installations pour embarcations. En juin, le ministre de la Défense, Khaled Sehili, avait présenté ce projet comme l’un des moyens de renforcer la capacité opérationnelle des forces navales d’élite ainsi que le rôle de la Tunisie en tant que centre régional de formation militaire. Ce même mois, le commandant des forces navales américaines en Europe et en Afrique, l’amiral George Wikoff, avait visité le centre en construction à Bizerte. I. B. items.title: Africa’s richest man helps fund $660m fuel pipeline between Ethiopia and Djibouti
items.description: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote has announced that he is helping to fund a new $660m (£500m) fuel pipeline between Ethiopia and Djibouti The project will include a 120km- (75 mile-) pipeline connecting Djibouti’s Damerjog port to a distribution facility in Dewele, Ethiopia, as well as storage capacity of about 400 million litres. It is expected to begin operations within 18 months. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said the pipeline, which would be a joint venture between Dangote and Ethiopia, is expected to reduce the time needed to transport fuel from Djibouti’s port to the Ethiopian capital, Addis Ababa, from five days to one. The first phase will transport key petroleum products, including jet fuel, diesel and petrol. Speaking at the ground-breaking ceremony, Dangote, Africa’s richest man, said the project would strengthen Ethiopia’s energy security and make its fuel supply chain more resilient. Landlocked Ethiopia relies heavily on Djibouti’s port for imports, including petroleum products. The new infrastructure is expected to reduce pressure on existing transport systems supporting industries, including transport, aviation, agriculture and construction. Djibouti is also expected to benefit from increased port activity, job creation and higher government revenues. The project is part of Dangote’s wider expansion of infrastructure and manufacturing businesses across Africa. Dangote Cement has production capacity of about 55 million tonnes a year, while his oil refinery in Nigeria currently has capacity to process 700,000 barrels of crude a day and is seeking to double that to 1.4 million barrels a day. The refinery recently listed 4.1 billion ordinary shares on the Nigerian stock exchange, aiming to raise about $1.63bn (£1.2bn). In Kenya, the company is due to break ground next week on a proposed 700,000-barrel-a-day crude oil refinery in Lamu.

items.title: Police declare major incident at UK's Fairford airbase, used by US air forces
items.description: British police said on Sunday they had arrested several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act and the army was examining a number of vehicles after security was stepped up at a British airbase used by US air forces in southwest England. The British government gave authorisation to the US to use RAF Fairford to carry out strikes on Iranian missile sites that are attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz . A Reuters eyewitness said armed police were blocking access to the main gate of the base. Around 30 emergency vehicles, including police cars, ambulances and fire engines, were stationed in the village of Fairford near the base. “A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident. It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act,” Gloucestershire police said in a statement, referring to a village near the airbase. “The Army’s specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles.” A spokesperson for the US Air Force said they would not discuss specific force protection measures. “The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families,” the spokesperson said. “We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families.” Prime Minister Andy Burnham was being kept updated on the incident, a government spokesperson said. “We are grateful to the emergency services, who have acted quickly to detain several suspects and put measures in place to keep the community safe,” the spokesperson said. “It would be inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing.” Defence Minister Wes Streeting thanked “emergency and specialist teams” deployed to the scene. “We can be reassured that this is being dealt with,” he said on X. Fairford is the UK base of the 501st Combat Support Wing, a US air force administrative support wing. Personnel there would “remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families” a statement said. The MP for the area, Roz Savage, described the situation as “worrying”. “I have contacted the police for further updates and I’ve been told that it is believed the incident is contained,” she said on X. Britain said in July its armed forces were ready to protect the country from any attack after Iran’s Revolutionary Guards issued a warning not to allow US bombers to fly from Fairford. British ministers have also briefed providers of critical infrastructure of the threat posed by Russia, with the government increasingly concerned about possible sabotage operations and cyberattacks. Russia denies mounting hybrid attacks on Western nations.

items.title: Nuit sanglante à Johannesburg et au Cap : une double fusillade de masse fait au moins 27 morts
items.description: La nuit a ete sanglante dans les villes de Johannesburg et du Cap, en Afrique du Sud. Une double fusillade de masse a fait au moins 27 morts et 26 blesses dans la nuit du 26 au 27 septembre, selon des bilans communiques par les services de police des deux villes. Johannesburg : un massacre dans une taverne La police du Gauteng a fait savoir que des inconnus armes ont perpetre une fusillade de masse dans une taverne d'Extension 3, a Wedela dans le West Rand, vers 21h30 heure locale (19h30 GMT), faisant 17 tues (13 hommes et quatre femmes) et 15 blesses. Le porte-parole des forces de l'ordre, le capitaine Tintswalo Sibeko, a indique que des suspects armes avaient ouvert le feu sur les clients de la taverne qui buvaient a l'exterieur de l'etablissement avant de faire irruption a l'interieur en continuant de tirer. Selon la police, les suspects etaient armes de fusils d'assaut AK-47 et de pistolets. Les assaillants auraient aussi fouille plusieurs clients pour s'emparer de leurs telephones portables avant de prendre la fuite a bord de deux vehicules non identifies. Les forces de l'ordre font egalement fait etat de deux vehicules incendies durant la fusillade. Le mobile de la fusillade demeure pour l'heure inconnu, rapporte la presse sud-africaine, mais la police a lance une chasse a l'homme et a mobilise une equipe de detectives, avec le support d'unites specialisees, pour traquer et arreter les auteurs de ce crime. La police locale a d'ailleurs ouvert 17 enquetes pour meurtre, 15 pour tentatives de meurtre et deux enquetes pour dommages materiels malveillants. Promettant d'arreter les coupables, le commissaire de la police du Gauteng a affirme : « Les criminels veulent faire en sorte que nous nous y habituions, c'est inacceptable. » Les services ont « reussi a obtenir des images nettes des suspects », a-t-il ajoute. Le Cap : une chasse a l'homme pour retrouver les auteurs d'un massacre dans un etablissement de nuit Dans une fusillade distincte, survenue le meme soir dans un etablissement de nuit a Lwandle, dans la ville du Cap, des hommes armes ont ouvert le feu sur les clients vers 1h46, heure locale (23h46 GMT) tuant cinq personnes sur les lieux, avant que cinq autres ne succombent a leurs blessures apres avoir ete transportees vers des etablissements medicaux. La fusillade a egalement fait 11 blesses, selon les forces de l'ordre. Selon le lieutenant-general de la police Sizakhele Dyantyi, commissaire de police du Cap-Occidental, une equipe multidisciplinaire, dirigee par des enqueteurs specialises dans la lutte contre les crimes violents, a ete mobilisee pour traquer et arreter les auteurs. « Les enqueteurs travaillent d'arrache-pied pour retrouver les auteurs de la fusillade, mais aucune arrestation n'a encore ete effectuee », a-t-il declare. Les causes du massacre demeurent encore inconnues, et la police a lance un appel a temoins pour aider a faire avancer l'enquete, promettant la stricte confidentialite dans le traitement des temoignages. L'Afrique du Sud affiche le taux d'homicides le plus eleve de la planete, avec pres de 60 personnes tuees chaque jour. Dans le cadre de la lutte contre la criminalite, l'armee a ete deployee en mars dernier pour soutenir les efforts de la police.

items.title: More than 70 terrorists killed across Balochistan in past 4 days: ISPR
items.description: More than 71 terrorists were killed in Shaban and other areas of Balochistan in the last 96 hours, the military’s media affairs wing said on Sunday. In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) recalled that based on credible intelligence, security forces had launched a “swift operation against the terrorists in Ziarat and surrounding areas” on Sept 21. “As the Pakistan Army’s operation progresses, more than 71 terrorists have been killed so far in Operation Shaban and other areas of Balochistan in [the] last 96 hours, delivering a serious blow to Indian-backed Afghan proxies,” the statement said. ISPR noted that Pakistan’s intelligence agencies had identified “multiple hideouts of Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khawarij and Fitna al Hindustan in the general area of Shaban, District Quetta, posing a threat to the local population”. The state uses the term Fitna al Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and refers to designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. During the operation in Shaban, security forces engaged the terrorists and cleared multiple hideouts, ISPR said. Following intense exchanges of fire, 33 “Indian-sponsored terrorists” were killed, with weapons, ammunition and explosives also recovered. Over the last 72 hours, the operation was intensified, resulting in the killing of 23 terrorists, the statement added. “Security forces have cleared a vast area and relieved local communities of the threat posed by Fitna al Khawarij and Fitna al Hindustan . The clearance operation is continuing until complete neutralisation of the threat,” ISPR stated. The number of terrorists killed in the Shaban operation had reached 13 on Sept 23, and then increased to 22 the next day. ISPR then recalled that 11 “Indian-sponsored terrorists” were killed in a separate intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Noshki on Sept 25 (Friday). Another six “ Fitna al Hindustan terrorists” were neutralised in Mand, with a large quantity of weapons and ammunition recovered, according to ISPR. The statement highlighted that the “Afghan Taliban regime’s involvement in terrorism activities in Pakistan, backed and sponsored by India, continues to cause loss of precious lives and threaten peace and stability”. The counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of “Azm-i-Istehkam”, approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, will continue with full resolve, ISPR declared. “Security forces and law enforcement agencies remain committed to eliminating foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” it reaffirmed. According to earlier ISPR statements, six terrorists had been killed during “pre-emptive” IBOs in Kech and Quetta West on Sept 22 and 23. Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist attacks in recent weeks, prompting security forces to intensify counter-terrorism operations. The number of terrorist attacks in the province increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August, according to a monthly assessment by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies. ‘Terrorism under foreign patronage’ President Asif Ali Zardari commended the security forces for their successful operations against terrorists of Fitna al Khawarij and Fitna al Hindustan in Balochistan. In a statement issued by the Presidency, he termed the clearance of numerous terrorist hideouts in the province a major success for the security forces. President Zardari emphasised that operations would continue until the complete eradication of terrorism “fueled by foreign patronage and assistance”. “The sacrifices and services of our security forces in the fight against terrorism are a source of pride for the entire nation,” the president added. Lauding the security forces’ professional skills, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi noted that “nefarious designs” of terrorists had been thwarted. “The brave soldiers of the security forces are a proud asset of the nation,” he said in a statement, adding that operations will continue till the eradication of Fitna al Khawarij and Fitna al Hindustan terrorists.

items.title: Security lapses at Utah campus where Charlie Kirk was killed, review says
items.description: An independent review has pointed to a number of security shortcomings at the Utah campus where conservative activist Charlie Kirk was shot dead last year. The report said Utah Valley University (UVU) did not carry out a proper written security assessment nor prepare an event action plan, deferring key decision-making about the event to Kirk’s conservative organisation Turning Point USA. It also said that Kirk’s aides had insisted on a outdoor venue, overriding security concerns from campus officials, who then failed to properly assess the dangers. The 31-year-old activist had been addressing thousands of people in an Orem campus courtyard when he was shot from a nearby rooftop on 10 September 2025. Kirk’s family said the report reinforced their concerns about how the event was managed. University officials had raised concerns in August 2025 about holding the event at a location surrounded by tall buildings and had suggested alternative venues, including some indoors, the report – published by UVU – says. “But a Turning Point representative insisted that Kirk speak at a campus courtyard because he had been there previously and the organisation was familiar with the location,” it adds. Despite the “significant protective operations considerations”, no line-of-sight assessment was documented in the planning process, the external consultants note. They also identified shortcomings in the co-ordination between university police and Kirk’s private security team. A proposed meeting between the university’s police chief and Turning Point security shortly before the event did not take place, the report said. The reviewers described the absence of a joint security briefing and walk-through as a missed opportunity to have identified risks, clarified responsibilities and considered additional security measures. However, the review concluded that no university employee or representative had acted in bad faith or shown “willful and wanton disregard” for anyone’s safety. Kirk’s family has previously accused the university of serious security failures and has filed a wrongful-death notice, a step that can precede legal action. The family’s lawyer, Brett Parkinson, said the independent report released on Friday backed up the concerns raised by Kirk’s loved ones. “The buck stopped with UVU leadership and law enforcement,” Parkinson said in a statement to the Associated Press. “Justice for Charlie and his family requires true accountability for UVU’s fatal shortcomings that day.” When asked for comment on the findings, Turning Point USA referred to Parkinson’s statement. The review makes numerous recommendations aimed at improving security for major campus events. UVU President Jon Anderson said the university must “learn from the findings of this review, and follow through on its recommendations”. It has previously been reported that the campus police failed to conduct security procedures that are common practice at US high-profile events, including flying a drone to monitor rooftops or security screening like bag checks and metal detectors. Kirk had been debating UVU students about US mass shootings, as part of a series of events across different university campuses, when he was shot in the neck shortly after noon. He was rushed to hospital but later pronounced dead. His alleged killer, Tyler Robinson, has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder in connection with Kirk’s death. Prosecutors are seeking the death penalty.

items.title: White House bars CNN from travelling with Trump on Air Force One
items.description: Broadcaster CNN has been barred from travelling with US President Donald Trump on Air Force One for a trip to Tennessee on Saturday. The move is the latest in a battle between the White House and the media after it was forced to lift its ban on some news outlets. CNN was scheduled to fly with Trump for his trip to Tennessee for a college American football game until a note released on Friday night by the White House did not list the broadcaster on the media schedule. The BBC has requested comment from the White House. CNN has reported that no other outlet was listed as replacing them in the president’s tentative schedule. Last week, Trump banned CNN, Politico and MS NOW journalists from the White House after accusing them of writing “fiction or lies” about his administration. All three media outlets said they were pursuing legal action and accused Trump of violating their constitutional rights to free speech and freedom of the press. Four television networks that have a daily rotation of White House coverage alongside CNN – ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC – had paused their broadcasts of the president in solidarity with the banned outlets. The White House then launched its own streaming channel, Trump TV, ahead of the UN General Assembly in New York. A federal judge has since ruled that Trump barring news outlets from the White House was likely unconstitutional and that the administration had to let them back in, at least for now. However, the White House still denied entry to some CNN and MS NOW reporters assigned to cover arrivals at a state dinner for Chinese leader Xi Jinping on Thursday. In a series of online posts on Saturday, Trump criticised the CNN and other media outlets dubbing them “fake news”. “FAKE NEWS SHOULD NOT BE ALLOWED IN THE WHITE HOUSE,” he said. A White House communications account earlier posted on X that “contrary to what the Fake News wants you to believe, they don’t just get to have free rein into every part of the White House, every event and every press call”. Regular US television coverage resumed on Friday after White House officials allowed reporters entry. The president is set to attend a football game between University of Tennessee vs University of Texas College at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville from midday local time on Saturday.

items.title: Change : le dirham se déprécie face au dollar et à l'euro
items.description: Bank Al-Maghrib (BAM) a fait savoir que durant la semaine du 17 au 23 septembre 2026, le dirham s’est déprécié de 0,3% face à l’euro et de 1,5% vis-à-vis du dollar américain. Dans son récent bulletin des indicateurs hebdomadaires, BAM précise qu’au cours de cette période, aucune opération d’adjudication n’a été réalisée sur le marché des changes. Les avoirs officiels de réserve se sont établis à 503 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) au 18 septembre, en hausse de 0,6% par rapport à la semaine précédente et de 21% en glissement annuel. Concernant les interventions de BAM, elles ont totalisé, au cours de la même période, 149,6 MMDH en moyenne quotidienne. Ce volume se répartit entre des avances à 7 jours pour un montant de 54,2 MMDH, des pensions livrées à plus long terme (48,5 MMDH) et des prêts garantis (46,9 MMDH). Sur le marché interbancaire, le volume quotidien moyen des échanges s'est élevé à 3,5 MMDH et le taux interbancaire s'est situé à 2,25%. Lors de l'appel d'offres du 23 septembre (date de valeur le 24 septembre), la Banque centrale a injecté un montant de 63,7 MMDH sous forme d'avances à 7 jours. Côté Bourse, le MASI s'est apprécié de 0,3% au cours de la période allant du 18 au 23 septembre 2026, portant sa contre-performance depuis le début de l'année à -4,3%. Cette évolution reflète notamment des progressions de 6,8% pour l'indice des « Mines » et de 1,2% pour celui des « Télécommunications ». En revanche, les indices se sont repliés de 1% pour le « Bâtiment et matériaux de construction », de 1,8% pour l' »Agroalimentaire et production », de 2,4% pour les « Distributeurs » et de 1,7% pour les « Assurances ». Pour ce qui est du volume des échanges, il est revenu, d'une semaine à l'autre, de 1,6 MMDH à 1,3 MMDH, réalisé principalement sur le marché central actions. The post Change : le dirham se déprécie face au dollar et à l'euro appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Navy sustains pressure on petroleum theft, recovers 33,800 ltrs in Rivers
items.description: The Nigerian Navy has recovered 33,800 litres of petroleum products in the Niger Delta amid its sustained pressure on crude oil theft and other illegal refining activities under Operation DELTA SENTINEL. This is contained in an operational report by the Director of Naval Information, Capt. Abiodun Folorunsho, made available to journalists on Sunday in Abuja. Folorunsho said the operation was led by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) SOROH, a unit under Operation DELTA SENTINEL, on Friday. He said that operatives acting on credible intelligence discovered and deactivated two illegal refining sites at Ogbogolo Community in Ahoada West Local Government Area of Rivers. “The operation led to the recovery of about 28,520 litres of illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) and 5,280 litres of stolen crude oil, totalling approximately 33,800 litres of petroleum products,” he said. He also said that the operation led to the discovery of 48 sacks, three dugout pits, two kegs and three cooking drums used for the storage and processing of the products. He said no arrests were made as the perpetrators fled the area on sighting naval personnel. “The latest operation reflects the efficiency of the navy’s strategy of persistent surveillance, intelligence-led operations and targeted disruption of the infrastructure and networks that sustain crude oil theft,” he said. He quoted the CNS, Vice Adm. Idi Abbas, as directing formations and units to maintain the pressure on the criminal network. The CNS instructed personnel to deny criminal networks the freedom of action, protect critical oil and gas infrastructure and create a more secured operating environment for legitimate economic activities in the Niger Delta. Abbas reaffirmed the navy’s commitment to leveraging its maritime domain awareness capabilities, credible intelligence and collaboration with relevant security agencies and host communities to consolidate the gains “These efforts are integral to the navy’s contribution towards securing Nigeria’s energy resources, improving crude oil production and strengthening national economic security”, he said The post Navy sustains pressure on petroleum theft, recovers 33,800 ltrs in Rivers appeared first on Vanguard News .
