Volleyball win brightens mixed day for Pakistan at Asian Games
items.description: Pakistan’s men’s volleyball team made an impressive start to their Asian Games campaign on Sunday, defeating Kazakhstan 3-1, while Noor Zaman beat compatriot Mohammad Ashab Irfan in an all-Pakistan squash playoff as the country’s medal tally rose to four bronze medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Games. Pakistan recovered from losing the third set to win 25-16, 25-22, 17-25, 25-20 in their Pool ‘A’ opener at the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Gymnasium. They will next face Uzbekistan on Monday before taking on hosts Japan in their final group match. Murad Khan was Pakistan’s leading scorer with 21 points, including 17 successful spikes and four blocks. Usman Faryad Ali contributed 14 points, Jehan Murad 11 and Musawer Khan nine as Pakistan dominated the attacking exchanges and finished with 92 total points against Kazakhstan’s 83. Pakistan’s blocking, however, remained an area of concern, with Kazakhstan registering 10 blocks to Pakistan’s seven. The Pakistanis were nevertheless more effective in attack, converting 55 of 114 spikes compared to Kazakhstan’s 48 of 113. The victory provides Pakistan with an early advantage in a pool that also includes Japan and Uzbekistan. Iran are the defending men’s champions, having won the previous three editions, while Pakistan’s group also contains the hosts, who will be among the contenders for the medals. At the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena, Noor completed a 3-0 victory over Ashab in the men’s singles third-place playoff, winning 11-7, 11-7, 11-3 in 26 minutes. The result did not alter the medal positions, with both players already assured of bronze after losing their respective semi-finals on Saturday. Their progress into the last four had ensured Pakistan’s return to the individual squash medal table after 17 years. Noor had gone down 3-0 to Malaysia’s Eain Yow Ng in the semi-final, while Ashab was beaten in straight games by India’s Abhay Singh. The two Pakistanis had nevertheless produced one of the country’s strongest campaigns at the Games, reaching the semi-finals of the individual event in the same edition for the first time since 2002. The two squash bronzes take Pakistan’s medal haul to four, alongside the bronze won by the women’s cricket team and Asim Khan’s bronze in the men’s 60kg MMA event. Pakistan had entered Sunday with two medals from the two events and added the squash medals after both players’ semi-final defeats. There was little joy for Pakistan in fencing, however, as the men’s épée team lost 7-5 to Qatar in the table-of-16 round at the Aichi Sky Expo. Mohammad Abdulali and Baryal Waqas Khan won individual relays, but Pakistan could not overturn Qatar’s advantage. In shooting, Rabia Kabir finished 41st in the women’s 25m pistol qualification after scoring 278-4x. Kishmala Talat, meanwhile, was listed as a non-starter. South Korea’s Yang Jiin topped the qualification with 292-11x, while Iran’s Haniyeh Rostamiyan and Vietnam’s Trinh Thu Vinh occupied the next two positions. Athletics offered a brighter note through Ansar Abbas, who qualified for the men’s long jump final with a personal-best 7.28 metres. He finished seventh in the qualification, with Uzbekistan’s Anvar Anvarov topping the standings at 8.00m and India’s Murali Sreeshankar qualifying second with 7.84m. Pakistan’s tennis campaign, which began on Sunday, produced mixed results. Aqeel Khan and Mohammad Shoaib progressed from the men’s doubles first round with a 6-2, 6-0 victory over Mongolia’s Mandakh Davaadash and Sonompuntsag Enkhjargal. The Pakistani pair dominated the match, winning 54 points to their opponents’ 23. Mahin Aftab Qureshi, however, was eliminated from the women’s singles after losing 6-1, 6-1 to Thailand’s Patcharin Cheapchandej. The Thai player won 54 points to Qureshi’s 24 and converted six of seven break-point opportunities. The day’s volleyball success came as Pakistan’s hockey and cricket campaigns moved closer to important fixtures. The hockey side, which had opened the competition with a series of victories, suffered its first defeat of the Games against Malaysia on Saturday, going down 5-4. The team will next face Oman on Monday with a place in the semi-finals at stake. Pakistan’s men’s cricket team will also begin its campaign on Monday when it takes on Hong Kong in the quarter-final. The side, led by Sahibzada Farhan, trained in Nisshin on Sunday but its session was affected by overnight rain and a wet outfield. For Pakistan, the coming days will therefore carry greater medal significance. Arshad Nadeem and Mohammad Yasir are also scheduled to compete in the men’s javelin final on Monday, giving the contingent another major medal opportunity.

items.title: «Le Joola» a sombré, des centaines de passagers « partis avec les vagues »
items.description: Dans la nuit du 26 au 27 septembre 2002, Le Joola sombrait au large de la Gambie, emportant avec lui des centaines de vies. Au lendemain du drame, Le Soleil racontait la stupeur, la douleur et les premières opérations de secours, tout en posant déjà la question des responsabilités. Vingt-quatre ans après, ses archives font revivre les heures sombres d’une tragédie nationale. Maître Abdoulaye Wade, qu’on sait vigoureux et à l’aise devant n’importe quel micro, apparaît dans une photo la tête un peu baissée, le regard perdu, cherchant on ne sait quel mot. Dans une autre image, son Premier ministre d’alors, Mame Madior Boye, parle. Son air est grave. Autre image, autres personnes, une foule d’anonymes. Eux aussi, synthétisant les mines de Wade et Boye. Autre image : une dame effondrée en larmes, dans les mains d’une autre. Autre image : une dame, dont les larmes sont recueillies par les mains d’une autre. Telles sont, montées les unes sur les autres, les images avec lesquelles Le Soleil des samedi 28 et dimanche 29 septembre 2002 illustre la tragédie nationale. Le bateau «Le Joola» a sombré. Quand ? Dans la nuit du 26 au 27. Où ? Au large de la Gambie. Comment ? « À la suite d’une tempête ». Pour quel bilan ? Selon celui « encore provisoire, donné par Mme le Premier Ministre, Mame Madior Boye, lors de sa visite au Port autonome de Dakar, il y aurait 41 décès et 32 rescapés sur les 796 passagers au bord du bateau ». C’est par ces informations et le papier de Kankoué Nouwodjro que Le Soleil ouvrait la série d’articles consacrés au naufrage du Joola. « Un lourd silence » À Zinguinchor on a, le jeudi, attendu l’arrivée de voyageurs. Le vendredi, on a été pris de panique. Et ce vendredi sera qualifié de « noir », par la plume de Babacar Bachir Sané. Vers 10 heures, le nuage sombre de la nouvelle éclipse le soleil de Ziguinchor. L’info centrale est là, les versions du comment divergent, et les gens veulent en avoir le cœur net. « C’est dans une telle atmosphère que l’embarcadère du bateau et la capitainerie du port de Ziguinchor ont été envahis par les curieux et les parents des passagers du «Joola» qui a quitté la veille, à 13 heures, la ville de Ziguinchor, pour sa troisième rotation Dakar-Ziguinchor, depuis le dix septembre », écrivait alors M. Sané, dont le titre de l’article portait l’épithète « fatale » associée à « rotation ». Un « Vendredi noir à l’embarcadère de Ziguinchor », oui, M. Sané. « Une journée de désolation à Dakar », oui, Ibrahima Ndiaye. Et, comme connectés par le même sentiment de… (on cherchera le mot des années encore !), les Dakarois ont agi comme ceux de la capitale du Sud. Le 27 septembre 2002, « dès l’annonce de la nouvelle, le marché du port a été pris d’assaut par des milliers de personnes en provenance de tous les horizons de la ville capitale », écrivait Ndiaye, qui a couché sur les colonnes du quotidien national « la désolation et la consternation » des uns et des autres. L’une et l’autre n’ont pas été qu’écrites. Elles ont aussi été photographiées puis documentées sur une page entière du « Soleil ». Amassés, les gens. Et des têtes distinctes, comme celle de Landing Savané. Et, peut-être, les eaux avaient-elles averti. Et, peut-être un signe avait-il été donné. « Mauvais présage ou fort hasard » ? On ne saura jamais ! On sait seulement ceci : « La mer a emporté une personne au Port de Ziguinchor, au moment où le transbordeur le Joola procédait à l’embarquement des passagers pour sa dernière rotation Dakar-Ziguinchor-Dakar ». Mais, Babacar Bachir Sané, qui aurait deviné que ce fait rapporté après, dans son papier, aurait pu être considéré comme un signe des eaux ! Le fait, chanté plus tard par Dread Maxim, reste que « la faucheuse, une fois de plus, a frappé fort » et que les autres « sont partis avec les vagues ». La nouvelle avait donc de quoi ralentir la démarche de Maître Wade. Elle avait de quoi imposer « un lourd silence », lorsque Mame Madior Boye, le général Mamadou Niang (ministre de l’Intérieur), Youba Sambou (ministre des Forces armées) recevaient le President Wade à sa descente d’avion, de retour de voyage. Son « nous allons faire toute la lumière » sera recueilli par Mbaye Sarr Diakhaté pour «Le Soleil». Sans doute, le Ciel avait pour Sa part recueilli des faisceaux de prières pour le repos de ceux qui « sont partis avec les vagues ». Le Sénégal a prié : « Un deuil national de trois jours décrété », titrait M. Diakhaté dans un encadré. Où, reprenant le Premier ministre, il a été dit ça : « Les pluies et le vent se sont conjugués, c’est un phénomène naturel à la suite d’une tempête que le bateau s’est renversé ». Mais, où l’auteur de l’article a aussi écrit ça : « À l’arrêt depuis août 2001 à cause d’une panne d’un de ses moteurs, le navire avait repris ses rotations le 10 septembre dernier ». Pluies et vent… Toutefois, « la faute est-elle seulement à la tempête ? », s’interrogeait Malick M. Diaw. Son texte est ponctué de points d’interrogation. Ce qui ne l’empêche pas d’émettre une certitude, qui est que ce Joola « n’avait pas sa place en mer et moins encore avec près de 800 hommes, femmes et enfants à bord ». Incidents quasi récurrents Car, argumente M. Diaw, « c’est un secret de polichinelle que l’état du bâtiment s’était, au fil des ans, dégradé, émaillé qu’il était d’incidents quasi récurrents qui avaient conduit à son immobilisation pendant près d’un an ». Rappel : « la mer a emporté une personne au Port de Ziguinchor, au moment où le transbordeur «Le Joola» procédait à l’embarquement des passagers pour sa dernière rotation Dakar-Ziguinchor-Dakar ». Ça a valeur d’alerte ? Qui sait, Babacar Bachir Sané ! Mais ça, on sait, on savait, et le papier de Aliou Ba l’a bien relevé : « L’avarie qui a coûté la vie à des centaines de Sénégalais n’est pas la première que le bateau a connue depuis sa mise en service. Il y a un peu plus d’un an, le navire avait disparu en pleine mer, avant d’apparaître au large de Ziguinchor après des heures d’angoisse ». Mais, ce qui est arrivé est arrivé. Après le mal, il a fallu agir. Le stagiaire Joseph Sène annonçait ainsi que le ministre de l’Intérieur avait déclenché le Plan national d’organisation des secours (Orsec). L’état-major général de l’Armée fera, pour sa part, déclencher l’alerte Sar (Secours, Assistance et Recherche). Une cellule de crise sera ainsi mise sur pied, et placée sous l’autorité de Mame Madior Boye. On y retrouve les ministres des Forces armées, de la Justice, de l’Intérieur, du Développement social et de la Solidarité nationale, celui des Mines, de l’Énergie et de l’Hydraulique, celui de la Santé et de l’Action publique, entre autres. Dans une synthèse de D. Sarr Niang, on apprend en plus qu’« un dispositif d’accueil et de secours a été mis en place ». Et, que « tous les hôpitaux de Dakar et l’hôpital de Kaolack ont été réquisitionnés », tandis que « les moyens médicaux militaires et personnels et en matériels sont mis à la disposition des autorités militaires et civiles responsables de l’organisation des secours »… Pluies et vent ? État délabré d’un bâtiment ? Un fait, constant : les autres « sont partis avec les vagues » et d’un peu partout, les journalistes du Soleil ont recueilli les maux des populations. « La consternation dans le Fouladou » se lisait dans le journal à travers les lignes de Moussa Sadio. À travers les lignes de Mamadou Cissé, c’est la « tristesse à Louga » qu’on lisait. Dans ces conditions, Podor ne pouvait qu’annuler ses journées culturelles, tel que le rapportera Ibrahima Khaliloulah Ndiaye. Par Moussa Seck

items.title: Pope praises young people’s ‘energy and commitment’ at huge open-air Mass in Paris
items.description: Pope Leo XIV has praised the “enthusiasm, energy and commitment” young people bring to the Catholic Church as dense crowds attended an open-air Mass in Paris. An estimated 700,000 people had gathered for the Mass celebrated by the Pope from a special altar on the Place de la Concorde, on the second day of his four-day visit to France. It began after the pontiff rode down the Champs-Élysées Avenue waving to crowds from his open-topped popemobile. Many senior politicians attended the Mass. On Friday, the Pope met French President Emmanuel Macron. During Saturday’s Mass, the Pope told worshippers that Catholics should not keep their faith to themselves but “let it overflow so that those you meet may be refreshed”. The leader of the Catholic Church also addressed young people in his speech, describing them as “today’s Church”. “How beautiful it is to see your enthusiasm, energy and commitment, and the joy you bring to Christian communities,” he said. After being welcomed by Macron on Friday, the Pope was joined by 80,000 young people at the Stade de France in northern Paris. Macron did not attend Saturday’s event and will not be at any of the Pope’s Masses during his visit, largely to avoid appearing to breach France’s strict rules on the separation of Church and state. But the Mass was attended by Macron’s wife Brigitte and French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu. Several candidates for next year’s presidential election also attended. Marine Le Pen of the hard-right National Rally party and conservative Bruno Retailleau were both pictured at the Place de la Concorde ahead of the event, while centrists Édouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal were also spotted. Earlier on Saturday, the Pope met migrants and volunteers as he visited the Maison Bakhita centre, an association supporting refugees, and praised the organisation for inviting “us to see those who are invisible”. He also stressed the “fundamental role of women in building a civilisation of love”. The Pope issued a warning about the dangers of artificial intelligence (AI) at the start of his visit to France on Friday. Leo cautioned against “losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines” in wide-ranging remarks to Church and state officials at the Élysée Palace. Large crowds are expected throughout the remainder of the pontiff’s trip, which the Church believes reflects a growing spirituality among the French and other Europeans. Late on Saturday the Pope flew to south-western town of Lourdes. He prayed at its famous sanctuary, where he will celebrate a Mass on Sunday which 150,000 people have signed up to attend. The Pope will be in the north-eastern city of Metz on Monday to pay tribute to Robert Schuman (1886-1963), a founding father of the European Union and a fervent Catholic who is a candidate for beatification – a formal recognition that a person is believed to have entered heaven. Born in Chicago in 1955, Pope Leo XIV was originally called Robert Prevost – a French name. His paternal grandmother was born in Le Havre in Normandy in 1894. When she married in the US many years later, she and her Italian husband took the name Prevost, which had been her mother’s maiden name.

items.title: The Kennedy Center Is the Most Terrifying Building in America
items.description: Don’t you dare go inside the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts! It’s much too dangerous. They have had murders there for 39 straight years —every night, and some matinees too. And they still haven’t caught the culprit. Nightly murders, with groups of middle schoolers sitting there, applauding. Murders in a hair salon, of all places! Sheer madness. It is not just the murder capital of Washington. Revolutions happen there, frequently. They built a barricade on one of the stages and tried to take down the whole French government. And they sang the whole time. This is the kind of thing that the Kennedy Center harbors and abets. They shot Alexander Hamilton there, not just once, but nightly, to make sure he was really dead. People went Into the Woods and got trampled by a giant. A rat king danced there. Valkyries rode there. Fairies forced people to fall in love, then out of love. It all happened in this building. The falling ceiling is the least of anyone’s concerns. Everything else about this place is far more threatening. And it’s not just murders and revolutions and dancing rodents. Horrifying transformations happened. They tested out new technologies there, called “plays.” (They even tested a couple of mine .) People got handed sheets of paper to read from and stood behind music stands and became other people . A very dangerous device, the play, and the Kennedy Center encouraged it. The most diabolical thing was that you did not always need to pay for these things. They just gave them away, free, every afternoon, for decades, to anyone who wanted to come in and watch. They gave them away online too! And nobody prevented this! This place encouraged other, equally frightening things. Dance, music. These performers didn’t even speak with words, just moved their bodies around and blew wind through metal tubes and reeds and scratched at strings—and people left the room in tears. What was the music saying? What were the bodies saying? The audience seemed to understand, but there were no words to help them. If people can communicate like this, then how can speech be properly controlled? If people can understand one another just by scratching a bow across taut strings—perhaps this is a form of witchcraft. No place that tolerates it must be permitted to stand. A blue figure stood guard outside. Dancing? Kicking? There was ambiguity, and that was scary. Sometimes people recorded podcasts there. Sometimes they watched movies on the lawn outside. Sometimes they played the tuba. They gathered together and experienced things together, and that, we can agree, was dangerous. There was comedy and drama and voices you only dreamed of hearing in person. There were discussions and readings. People learned things of which they had been previously unaware. There were chimes and fountains and overpriced intermission snacks. They dared to invite children into this place too. They dared to sit them down and tell them stories, on a stage. Do you know what a story can do to a mind? Do you know how long that story can linger before exploding into life, decades later? The Kennedy Center is the deadliest condemned building in America. For 55 years, people have been going in and coming out changed . Not physically, not visibly, but inside, carrying dangerous stories with them. Carrying music that could sustain them through times of trial, or the encouragement of shared laughter, or the seditious sense that they were not alone. Root it out! Stamp it out! Knock it down with a wrecking ball! This building is much too dangerous.

items.title: The Hidden State Russia Is Building Inside Ukraine
items.description: T he world has watched Russia’s war against Ukraine largely through the movement of its front lines. But behind those lines, Moscow is building something more durable: a hidden state inside Ukraine. Across the Russian-occupied parts of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson, Russian institutions are steadily replacing Ukrainian ones and reshaping the routines of everyday life. Schools teach Russian curricula. Official documents, such as mandated Russian passports, tie residents to the Russian state. Russian systems govern access to housing and public services. On June 13, Vladimir Putin told Russian officials that Moscow’s task is to unify these Ukrainian territories into a legal, economic, educational, cultural, and information space under Russia by 2030. The objective is permanence: to make Ukrainian civic life hard to maintain and Russian rule hard to undo. This agenda predates the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Crimea became an early laboratory for it after Russia annexed the peninsula, in 2014. Moscow quickly imposed Russian citizenship on Crimeans and made documentation—most commonly passports—necessary for employment and access to basic services. It introduced Russian law in Crimea and replaced Ukrainian institutions with Russian ones. [ Read: Russia’s real strategy in Europe ] The Ukrainian territories occupied after the 2022 invasion have been more difficult to wrangle. The eastern provinces house major industrial assets, hundreds of thousands of people who consider themselves Ukrainians, and active resistance networks. Moscow initially relied heavily on occupation administrations, military coercion, and improvised measures. Gradually, however, it has introduced a more durable architecture to yoke the territories to the Russian state. R ussia has extended the dominion of its administrative state across occupied Ukraine. Russian federal courts claim jurisdiction there, and Russian taxation, migration, security, and military apparatuses hold authority. In 2025, Moscow integrated the occupation administrations into the monitoring software it calls the Governor’s Dashboard, which keeps track of local construction projects, budgets, and administrative compliance in real time across Russia. One aim of this integration is to sever occupied Ukraine from Kyiv and pull its residents firmly under Russian oversight and control. Ukrainians are required to get Russian passports, without which they cannot receive pensions, get jobs, collect state benefits, or pursue studies. They can’t even use phones: Local mobile operators now require Russian identity documents for SIM cards. A young man who left Kherson because he feared being detained for his pro-Ukrainian views, or conscripted into the Russian military, described how he was forced to obtain a Russian passport. “They put a gun to my head,” he told us. Like other Ukrainians we spoke to from these territories, he asked that his name be withheld for fear of retaliation against his loved ones. Many Ukrainians living under occupation have become convinced that independent Ukraine is unreachable. Russia took, replaced, or made unusable the Ukrainian documents that residents once had. Sophia, a 24-year-old from occupied Donetsk, told us that the occupation authorities repeatedly informed residents that Kyiv had abandoned them, and that only Moscow would issue them passports now. Without documents, Sophia felt trapped: Russia “was the only place I could legally go,” she said, even though she did not want to live there. To men aged 18 to 65, Russian citizenship brings military registration and punishment for noncompliance. From February 2022 to the end of 2025, in direct violation of international humanitarian law, the Russian army forcibly mobilized approximately 50,000 Ukrainians to fight against their own country. At the same time, Russia has been systematically expropriating Ukrainians’ property. Many who fled the territories under Russian occupation left real estate behind. Some of their homes have been classified as ownerless or unregistered, paving the way for their confiscation. Those who wish to retain their property must reregister it under Russian law by the end of the year. Doing so requires Russian citizenship and personally returning to the occupied territory. Since 2024, Russian authorities have confiscated , or identified for confiscation, at least 34,000 properties belonging to Ukrainian citizens. And they have begun allocating some of these homes to Russian citizens, whom they encourage to settle in occupied Ukraine, with the alleged goal of increasing the territories’ total number of Russians to 1 million by 2045. This year, occupation authorities began transferring plots of Ukrainian land to Russians, with preference given to servicemen and those who have signed military contracts. T he state that Moscow is building in occupied Ukraine is more isolated and poorer than the one from which it was wrenched. Since 2022, Moscow has worked to cut off the occupied regions from the Ukrainian information space by blocking independent media, restricting messaging services, and replacing the communications infrastructure with Russian-controlled networks. Hundreds of Ukrainian and independent websites are inaccessible, and residents struggle to access Telegram, WhatsApp, and VPNs. Since 2022, Moscow has poured billions of dollars into reconstructing occupied Ukraine. Officially these funds are meant to rebuild housing, roads, and public services. In reality, they have facilitated patronage and resource extraction. Moscow has built up infrastructure that supports Russian military objectives, while living conditions for civilians deteriorate . It has closed or repurposed about 90 percent of the industrial facilities in occupied Ukraine. Many of these Ukrainian factories have been absorbed into Russian defense production, and Moscow has commandeered mines, machine-building plants, metallurgical facilities, and chemical plants for military use. [ Read: Ukraine’s short-lived comeback ] Since 2023, Moscow has expanded road and port infrastructure to support military logistics and resource extraction. It has spent about $425 million on railroads, including new routes farther from the front lines to move ammunition and military equipment to its forces. Russia has also integrated the occupied ports of Mariupol and Berdyansk into its maritime network, using them to export grain, energy, minerals, and other products to Russia and elsewhere. In 2025 alone, Moscow exported more than 2 million tons of grain from occupied Ukraine. Russia’s militarization of the economy in these regions has left few jobs and low salaries for Ukrainians. One resident of occupied Luhansk told us that many men prefer to take temporary or unofficial work for one reason: “Official employment means going straight to the military-enlistment office.” The worsening economic situation has deepened social tensions, and many residents describe feelings of despair and a sense of “frozen time.” One person in Kherson spoke of “moral exhaustion” from the occupation. Another told us, “Those who live better are those collaborating with occupation authorities.” The Russians brought into the territories, meanwhile, are reportedly paid substantially more than locals. The Kremlin knows that the Ukrainians living under these conditions are potentially hostile. And so its occupation authorities have adopted what some of them call a “ preventive threat elimination ” approach, which assumes that most civilians are disloyal and treats even passive dissent as a security threat. Having Signal, Ukrainian apps and media, pro-Ukrainian Telegram channels, or suspicious contacts in your phone can attract scrutiny and, in some cases, lead to detention or beatings. From February 2022 to August 2025, according to the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, Russian occupation forces detained about 15,000 civilians, although the true number may be significantly higher. As a result, Ukrainians are self-censoring. Many remove Ukraine-related material from their devices or use a second phone while traveling. Some avoid speaking in public places for fear of being reported and detained. A resident living in occupied Zaporizhzhia told us, “There shouldn’t be anything unnecessary on your phone so there won’t be unnecessary questions.” A bout 1.6 million Ukrainian children live under occupation, and Russia has made their ideological education a state priority. The objective is to Russify them and shape them into future military recruits. Schools in the occupied areas stress hostility toward Ukraine and the West and glorify Russian national symbols. Teaching in the Ukrainian language is verboten . A resident of occupied Kherson told us that “anything that reminds people of Ukraine, even the colors, is strictly forbidden.” Volodymyr, a young man also from Kherson, told us that school officials and Russian representatives warned students against speaking freely, opposing Russian occupation, and maintaining contact with relatives in Ukraine or abroad. This year Moscow has introduced a new curriculum at all levels, from kindergarten through university, aimed at strengthening Russian identity and glorifying “defenders of the fatherland,” including participants in the war against Ukraine. At the same time, Moscow has expanded patriotic, military-linked youth groups into the occupied territories. Membership has grown rapidly. “They did not ask whether I wanted to join the Russian youth organization,” Volodymyr told us. Rather, he said, it was: “ You, you, you, and you—you must join today .” The Movement of the First, often described as the successor to the Soviet Pioneers, has more than half a million members in occupied Ukraine. Yunarmia, which Putin has called a “ school of life ,” has at least 44,000 members there. VOIN, a network of military sports-training and patriotic-education centers, has swept up at least 10,000 young people since 2024. These organizations operate under the close supervision of the Kremlin and even Putin himself. They introduce children, some as young as 6, and young adults to firearms, tactical medicine, drone piloting, survival skills, reconnaissance, and sniping. [ Read: The armored sarcophagus saving Ukrainian soldiers ] Oksana, a caregiver from Kherson, left the occupation with her family after pressure grew on her sons to enter Russia’s military system. She described schools where academic subjects had been pushed aside by militarization and indoctrination. “In the first place—military training. In second place—propaganda,” she told us. “From kindergarten, they already start teaching them to march.” For a child living under occupation, four years is enough time to reshape an identity—to learn or forget a language, and to set the course of education, friendships, and future plans. For those who have lived under Russian occupation since 2014, this is no longer a temporary disruption. It is the formative experience of their lives. A child who was 6 when Russia first occupied Crimea or parts of the Donbas is now an adult who has never known life under Ukrainian rule. The institutions Russia has built behind the front lines are hardening. For Russia, they are the groundwork of annexation. For Ukraine, they are an obstacle, even if Kyiv one day wins those territories back. Russian indoctrination and coercion could be a security problem that will outlast any cease-fire. And every passing year that Russian institutions endure increases the difficulty Ukrainians will have in restoring their country’s sovereignty, reconnecting their families, regaining their property, and providing young people with a meaningful sense of belonging.

items.title: ECOWAS Free Movement: Nigeria seeks balance between mobility, security
items.description: The Federal Government is seeking to balance the ECOWAS Protocol on Free Movement with national security concerns by improving the profiling, documentation and monitoring of people crossing its borders. The Director-General of the National Boundary Commission (NBC), Adamu Adaji, disclosed this in an exclusive interview with Newsmen in Abuja on Sunday. Adaji said free movement should not prevent authorities from knowing who enters or leaves the country. He said the ECOWAS Protocol permitted the movement of goods and persons, while border agencies remained responsible for monitoring activities within Nigeria’s territorial limits. “People who enter and leave should be properly profiled and documented, even though they have the right to free movement,” he said. According to him, authorities should know the identity of travellers and their reasons for entering the country. He said security agencies operating along border corridors should strengthen monitoring to ensure that legitimate movement did not create opportunities for criminal activities. Adaji identified terrorism, kidnapping and arms smuggling as among the security-related activities associated with Nigeria’s border areas. He said illegal routes remained a challenge, urging authorities to identify and profile people using such routes. The NBC boss called for efforts to reduce, minimise and eventually eliminate illegal crossings through improved surveillance and stronger inter-agency cooperation. He said Nigeria had promoted a Cross-Border Cooperation Platform to strengthen understanding, information sharing and intelligence exchange with neighbouring countries. Adaji said the platform was intended to encourage Nigeria and its neighbours to collaborate in securing their respective territories. He said effective border management required security agencies to use technology, including surveillance systems and cameras, to monitor difficult areas. The director-general also emphasised the importance of border communities in detecting and reporting activities that could threaten national security. He said communities should be supported with necessary infrastructure to encourage their cooperation with authorities and strengthen their sense of belonging. Adaji said border management should simultaneously support security, trade and lawful migration in line with the ECOWAS framework. He stressed that clearly defined boundaries would enable security agencies to monitor and manage activities without unnecessarily restricting legitimate cross-border movement. Adaji stressed that stronger coordination among agencies and neighbouring countries remained essential to achieving that balance. The post ECOWAS Free Movement: Nigeria seeks balance between mobility, security appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nyankamam residents benefit from free medical screening, healthcare outreach
items.description: Hundreds of residents in Nyankamam, a community in the Aowin Municipality of the Western North Region, have benefited from a free medical screening and healthcare outreach organised and funded by Lawyer Francis Yensu Appiah, the Western North Regional Director of the Legal Aid Commission. The exercise was designed to improve access to healthcare in rural and underserved communities by offering early detection of common illnesses, free medical consultations, essential medicines and health education. It also targeted children, women, the elderly and vulnerable residents who often face economic and logistical barriers to accessing health services. A team of medical doctors and healthcare professionals carried out a range of screenings, including blood pressure checks for hypertension, blood glucose testing for diabetes and body mass index (BMI) assessments. Residents were also tested for malaria using rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs), screened for Hepatitis B and examined for other common endemic conditions. The outreach further included one-on-one medical advice, free prescription drugs, basic treatments, essential vitamins and sensitisation sessions on preventive healthcare, proper nutrition, personal hygiene and lifestyle choices for managing non-communicable diseases. Speaking at the event, Lawyer Francis Yensu Appiah emphasised the close relationship between human rights, access to justice and the well-being of citizens. He said the right to legal protection cannot be fully enjoyed when people are burdened by preventable health problems. “Access to quality healthcare is a basic human right,” he stated. “While my primary mandate at the Legal Aid Commission is to ensure equal access to justice, justice cannot be fully enjoyed if our people lack good health.” He explained that the free medical screening was part of his personal commitment to giving back to communities in the Aowin Municipality and ensuring that financial hardship does not prevent people from receiving proper medical care. He also assured residents that the initiative was not a one-off intervention, but part of a broader effort to support communities in the Aowin Municipality whenever the need arises. The Chief of Nyankamam, together with community elders and beneficiaries, praised the initiative, describing it as timely, thoughtful and impactful. They noted that many residents in the area frequently delay routine medical check-ups because of the cost of treatment. According to them, the outreach brought much-needed care directly to the doorsteps of the people. Beneficiaries also expressed relief and gratitude for the free consultations, medications and early diagnosis of conditions such as hypertension and diabetes. Some said the exercise gave them an opportunity to learn about their health status for the first time, while others welcomed the advice they received on nutrition, hygiene and disease prevention. For many low-income households, the opportunity to access medical care without paying out of pocket was described as a major benefit. Dr Prince Ackah, a medical officer from the Sefwi Wiawso Government Hospital who participated in the screening, said the initiative reflected a growing shift towards preventive healthcare in rural communities in the Aowin Municipality. He explained that early detection of illnesses could help reduce complications, improve treatment outcomes and lessen the financial burden on families. He added that free screening exercises of this kind were especially important in communities where people often ignore symptoms until their conditions become severe. The outreach in Nyankamam, sponsored by Lawyer Francis Yensu Appiah, highlighted the broader value of community-based interventions by public servants and professionals who choose to go beyond their official duties. By combining legal service with social responsibility, Lawyer Francis Yensu Appiah has contributed to efforts aimed at improving the welfare of communities in the Aowin Municipality. The programme was received not only as a health intervention, but also as a gesture of solidarity and public-minded leadership. For residents of Nyankamam, the screening provided more than medical attention; it offered reassurance that their concerns were being seen and addressed.

items.title: Ghana, Boeing explore setting up regional aircraft maintenance hub
items.description: Ghana and American aircraft manufacturer, Boeing, are exploring the establishment of a regional Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) hub in the country to serve airlines operating across West Africa and the wider African continent. The proposal formed part of discussions between President John Mahama and senior Boeing executives in New York on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly. The proposed facility is expected to strengthen Ghana’s position in the regional aviation industry by providing aircraft maintenance and related technical services within the country. The discussions are also focused on using the proposed partnership to build local technical capacity through aviation training, skills development and technology transfer. President Mahama said Ghana’s engagement with Boeing should go beyond the acquisition of aircraft, stressing the need to develop a broader aviation ecosystem. “Ghana does not want its relationship with Boeing to be defined simply by the purchase of aircraft. We want a strategic partnership that helps us build an aviation ecosystem—creating skilled jobs, transferring technology, strengthening our industrial base and positioning Ghana as an aviation and logistics hub for West Africa. “As we Reset Ghana, we are looking for partners prepared to invest with us, build capacity with us and share in the prosperity we create. Boeing can be one of those strategic partners.” The proposed MRO hub could create opportunities for Ghanaian aviation engineers, technicians and other skilled professionals while reducing the need for airlines operating in the region to send aircraft abroad for certain maintenance services. The initiative is being discussed alongside plans to revive Ghana’s national carrier, with Boeing indicating that the national airline could return to the skies within approximately 18 months if the necessary structures and implementation arrangements are put in place.

items.title: Bangkok roads submerged as flood disaster declared
items.description: A flood emergency disaster has been declared across Bangkok after more than 300mm (12in) of rain fell since Thursday, leavingroads in the Thai capital submerged. On Sunday, Bangkok’s Metropolitan Authority said the rains have subsided, but canal water levels remain high. The city’s governor has warned that the flooding is not yet over. People have been urged to stay at home and those living close to the city’s network of canals have been advised to move their belongings to upper floors. Thunderstorms are common in Thailand at this time of year but extreme weather in recent days has inundated Bangkok’s drainage system, causing traffic chaos on roads that are already famously congested. Somkid Pheuk-ngam, a 67-year-old who lives near a canal just north of central Bangkok, told the AFP news agency: “The water keeps coming in. It’s hard to go out now. It’s like at my waist level now. “I cannot go anywhere. I have been closing my shop for two days now.” She said water levels in the city appeared to be worse than in 2011, when Bangkok was impacted by nationwide flooding. Hundreds were killed across Thailand then in an extreme weather event that lasted for three months. So far, no casualties have been reported in Bangkok from this latest flooding. The Thai Meteorological Service has forecast more heavy rain through the week, though the area of low pressure causing the downpours of recent days is expected to move towards central Thailand. All 50 of Bangkok’s districts were declared emergency zones. On Saturday, Chadchart Sittipunt, the city’s governor, said the east of the city had been hardest hit, AFP reported. He continued: “The rain keeps falling and we are doing our best. We are trying to pump the water out, but the water in canals are full… The risk areas are those who live near canals. Every canal is now filled.”

Four killed in helicopter crash near Montreal
items.description: Four people have died after a helicopter crashed in a small town 50km (31 miles) from Montreal, Quebec’s provincial police have told the BBC. Emergency services were called to Sainte-Brigide-d’Iberville shortly after 14:30 local time (19:30 BST) on Saturday afternoon, where they found the aircraft on fire and declared its occupants dead at the scene. The victims have not yet been identified but the aircraft appeared to be a private helicopter, Sergeant Audrey-Anne Bilodeau said. An investigation into the crash is being led by the Major Crime Unit of the Sûreté du Québec, working alongside crime scene technicians as well as investigators from the Transportation Safety Board of Canada. The crash site is located near the Rang des Écossais road off Highway 10, according to Bilodeau. In an emergency call, police were notified of a helicopter in distress that may have crashed and caught fire. An hour after the call, the fire at the site had been brought under control though officials were still working at the crash site just before 22:00 local time (03:00 GMT). The victims have not yet been identified and Sergeant Audrey-Anne Bilodeau said this process may “take a few days.”

items.title: Ghana could have national airline back in skies within 18 months – Boeing to Mahama
items.description: Ghana’s national airline could return to the skies within approximately 18 months, according to global aerospace giant Boeing. The indication follows high-level discussions between President John Dramani Mahama and senior Boeing executives in New York on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly. Boeing has expressed readiness to work closely with the Ghanaian government as it advances plans to revive the national carrier, saying the 18-month target could be achievable if the necessary structures and implementation arrangements are put in place. But President Mahama says Ghana’s ambition goes beyond simply acquiring aircraft for a new national carrier. “Ghana does not want its relationship with Boeing to be defined simply by the purchase of aircraft. We want a strategic partnership that helps us build an aviation ecosystem—creating skilled jobs, transferring technology, strengthening our industrial base and positioning Ghana as an aviation and logistics hub for West Africa. “As we Reset Ghana, we are looking for partners prepared to invest with us, build capacity with us and share in the prosperity we create. Boeing can be one of those strategic partners.” The discussions therefore focused on a broader aviation partnership that could support the national carrier while developing the infrastructure, skills and technical capacity needed to sustain the industry. Among the proposals is the establishment of a regional Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul, MRO, hub in Ghana to serve airlines operating across West Africa and the wider African continent. The talks also covered aviation training, skills development, technology transfer and the creation of high-value jobs for young Ghanaians. The proposed partnership forms part of President Mahama’s broader Reset Ghana agenda, which seeks to attract strategic international investment and position the country as a competitive gateway for trade, aviation and logistics in the region. For now, Boeing’s 18-month indication provides a potential timeline for the return of Ghana’s national carrier, but that target remains dependent on the government putting the required structures and implementation arrangements in place.

items.title: Kabiné Komara rend hommage à Sidya Touré : « J’ai toujours gardé un devoir de gratitude envers lui »
items.description: Dans un témoignage empreint d’émotion, l’ancien Premier ministre Kabiné Komara revient sur ses relations avec Sidya Touré, depuis leur rencontre en Côte d’Ivoire en 1990 jusqu’à leurs échanges sur les questions politiques guinéennes. Il rend hommage à un homme dont il salue la compétence et l’engagement, tout en adressant ses condoléances à sa famille et à ses proches. Message… L'annonce du décès de notre ancien Premier ministre Sidya Touré a déclenché une avalanche d'expressions de compassion et de témoignages poignants sur la carrière et le rôle politique de ce grand serviteur de l'État. Le fait que le Gouvernement ait publié un communiqué officiel vient donner une résonance plus juste à l'émotion de toute la Nation. Pour ma part, mes relations avec M. Sidya remontent à l'année 1990, au moment où il était Directeur de cabinet à la Primature ivoirienne. Je revenais d'un séminaire organisé à Yamoussoukro, auquel j'avais été convié par le cabinet du Premier ministre Alassane Ouattara, lorsqu'il m'invita chez lui. Il s'engagea à me soutenir, avec son ami Yomba Kandé , pour que je sois nommé Administrateur suppléant de la Banque africaine de développement (BAD), alors dirigée par M. Babacar Ndiaye. Ce qui fut fait. J'ai donc toujours gardé un devoir de gratitude envers lui. Mieux, j'ai continué à me servir de cette gratitude chaque fois que cela était nécessaire. Ainsi, lorsque je fus nommé Premier ministre par le Capitaine Moussa Dadis , je m'appuyais sur sa grande expertise pour l'élaboration du programme d'urgence du pays en matière d'électricité. Plus récemment, je me permettais, avec une fraternelle franchise, de le solliciter à Abidjan, où il s'était établi, pour qu'il prête une oreille attentive aux démarches du Premier ministre Bernard Goumou dans sa délicate mission de réunir les différents acteurs politiques autour d'un dialogue fécond, susceptible de permettre une sortie consensuelle de la période de transition entamée depuis septembre 2021. Comme le reconnaissent tous les témoignages rendus sur le riche parcours du Premier ministre Sidya Touré, il fut un homme d'une grande compétence, qui avait espéré accéder à la magistrature suprême du pays pour y imprimer une marque à la hauteur de ses convictions. En ce jour du 25 septembre 2026, il vient de tirer sa révérence, nous devançant tous vers là où nous finirons, tôt ou tard. En cette triste occasion, je présente mes condoléances les plus émues à sa famille, aux militants de son parti, l'UFR, à tous ceux qui l'ont côtoyé en Côte d'Ivoire et en Guinée, ainsi qu'au peuple guinéen tout entier. J'implore le Tout-Puissant et Miséricordieux Créateur de réserver à son âme une place de choix dans Son Paradis céleste. Amen. Kabiné Komara Ancien Premier ministre de Guinée L’article Kabiné Komara rend hommage à Sidya Touré : « J’ai toujours gardé un devoir de gratitude envers lui » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Floods and landslides kill 56 in India's Uttar Pradesh, 12 in Nepal over past three days
items.description: Heavy rain triggered floods and landslides across northern India and Nepal, killing at least 68 people over the past three days, disaster authorities said on Sunday. In India’s most populous state of Uttar Pradesh, 56 people have died over the past three days with more than 1,000 houses damaged, the relief commissioner’s office said in a statement. Neighbouring Nepal, already reeling under the catastrophic August 26 flood , was struck by a fresh wave of flooding and landslides that has killed 12 people since Thursday. “Since Thursday, 12 people have died in rain-related disasters like floods and landslides,” Shanti Mahat, spokesperson at Nepal’s disaster authority, told AFP , adding that seven more were missing. Scientists have warned in recent years of an increase in extreme weather events across South Asia, linking them to rising temperatures and changing climate patterns. The flooding in Nepal last month, triggered by a glacial mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border, has killed more than 1,400 people and left thousands missing. Uttar Pradesh, home to more than 240 million people, is frequently battered by rain and thunderstorms during the annual monsoon season from June to September. The latest deaths were reported during a spell of “exceptionally heavy rain” after a “depression over the Bay of Bengal moved inland and intensified rainfall across the region”, it said. The state recorded 66.5 millimetres of rain between Friday and Sunday, compared to the season average of 7.6mm, it added. The heavy rain caused extensive damage to crops, with farmers raising concerns over sowing delays in the upcoming season. In India’s eastern state of Odisha, over 70,000 people living in low-lying areas were evacuated after rivers swelled due to heavy downpours, NDTV news network reported. The rains have damaged bridges and culverts, forcing officials to shut down Devkund, a popular tourist spot in the state. Monsoon-related disasters are an annual occurrence across India after long summers when many parts of the country face water scarcity and drought.

items.title: Hamady Walaldé, le premier homme du Fouta (3/3)
items.description: « Hamady Walaldé » n’est pas un personnage historique au sens classique. C’est le nom donné par les chercheurs à un squelette humain mis au jour lors des fouilles, non loin de Boobhobé, à moins d’un kilomètre du village. Hamady, prénom peul, désigne traditionnellement l’aîné d’une famille ; il a été associé au nom du site. Walaldé est l’un des sites archéologiques majeurs de la moyenne vallée du fleuve Sénégal. Des fouilles y ont été conduites à la fin des années 1990, notamment dans le cadre du programme régional Middle Senegal Valley, avec des chercheurs comme Hamady Bocoum, Alioune Dème et Susan McIntosh. Elles ont montré qu’une communauté d’agropasteurs maîtrisant déjà le fer s’était installée sur ce site d’environ cinq hectares entre 800 et 550 avant J.-C., et y était restée jusque vers 400-200 avant J.-C. Les niveaux les plus anciens témoignent d’une transition vers la métallurgie du fer, encore associée à des outils en pierre taillée ; les couches plus récentes ont livré d’abondants résidus de forge et de fonte, scories et tuyères. Le cuivre venu d’Akjoujt atteste d’échanges à longue distance. Le site a également livré de la céramique et une série de sépultures à ocre rouge. En juillet 2015, ce fossile a été présenté au public dans un documentaire du laboratoire d’archéologie du département d’Histoire de l’Ucad, Le Premier Homme du Fouta : Hamady Walaldé, qui le présente comme le plus ancien occupant connu de la région. La médiatisation a suscité des débats. Certains ont mis en garde contre toute conclusion hâtive sur l’appartenance ethnique du défunt, rappelant que les premiers habitants attestés du Fouta ne seraient pas nécessairement peuls et pourraient être rattachés à d’autres groupes, sérères ou bambaras par exemple. D’autres ont souligné l’ancienneté du site, que la tradition orale relie à l’histoire de Mawndou Walaldé, cité ancienne dont les vestiges se trouvent aujourd’hui à Tékane, en Mauritanie, et où auraient été inhumés d’anciens rois et dignitaires. Par Oumar Boubacar NDONGO (Textes)

items.title: Médias : Le vice-président de la PRA-UEMOA-Guinée, le Nigérien, Ibrahima Manzo Diallo, salue la longévité et la crédibilité du média
items.description: En marge de sa visite de travail en Guinée, le vice-président de la Plateforme des Régulateurs de l’Audiovisuel des pays membres de l’UEMOA et de la Guinée (PRA-UEMOA-Guinée) et président de l’Observatoire National de la Communication du Niger (ONC-Niger), Ibrahima Manzo Diallo, a visité ce samedi 26 septembre 2026 les locaux de Guineenews, premier site d’information en Guinée, créé en octobre 1997. Après plusieurs heures de travaux à la Haute Autorité de la Communication (HAC), le responsable nigérien et sa délégation se sont rendus au siège de Guineenews, situé à Almamya, dans la commune de Kaloum à Conakry. C’est aux environs de 17 heures que la délégation nigérienne, conduite par Amadou Touré, commissaire et secrétaire général de la HAC, et accompagnée de plusieurs commissaires de l’institution, a fait son entrée dans les locaux du média. Accueillie par le personnel de Guineenews, la délégation a été reçue par Laye Moro Camara, l'adjoint du chef de bureau. Ce dernier a pris la parole au nom du président du bureau coordinateu général de Guineenews, Amadou Tham Camara. La présence d’Ibrahima Manzo Diallo dans les locaux de Guineenews a été marquée par une visite guidée des différents bureaux et espaces de travail du média. L’occasion pour le vice-président de la PRA-UEMOA-Guinée de découvrir de près l’environnement dans lequel travaillent les journalistes et les autres collaborateurs du site. Ibrahima Manzo Diallo : « Je lis Guineenews depuis plusieurs années » À l'occasion de cette visite, le président de l’ONC-Niger n’a pas manqué d’exprimer son appréciation, rappelant qu’il suit Guineenews depuis plusieurs années à partir du Niger. « Il y a plusieurs années depuis le Niger, je lis Guineenews. À l'époque, l'internet n'était pas aussi partout dans le monde. Et voir jusqu'ici que le site est toujours fonctionnel, cela mérite des félicitations. Ce qui fait la résistance d'une plateforme numérique, d'un site Internet, c'est surtout la crédibilité et la fiabilité de l'information qu'ils donnent. Vous le faites si bien, et je vous encourage au nom de l'Observatoire National de la Communication du Niger », a-t-il salué. Pour le responsable nigérien, cette longévité constitue un élément à saluer dans un paysage médiatique marqué par de profondes mutations technologiques. Il a également profité de cette étape pour remercier la HAC et son président pour les échanges tenus au cours de sa visite en Guinée. « ​Je remercie beaucoup la Haute Autorité de la Communication, le président Yacine Diallo ainsi que les commissaires. Après tous les entretiens qu'on a eus ce matin, on a su que vous êtes ensemble », a-t-il apprécié. « Le régulateur est surtout l'accompagnateur des médias » La rencontre avec les responsables et le personnel de Guineenews a également permis à Ibrahima Manzo Diallo d’évoquer les rapports entre les organes de régulation et les médias. Alors que les régulateurs sont parfois perçus comme des structures essentiellement chargées de contrôler ou de sanctionner les médias, le président de l’ONC-Niger défend une approche davantage fondée sur l’accompagnement. « On dit régulateur, beaucoup de gens parlent du gendarme de la presse, mais non : le régulateur est surtout l'accompagnateur des médias. ​Donc on va cheminer comme ça, le régulateur et les médias. On va cheminer ensemble et bâtir une citadelle qui va prospérer dans le temps », a-t-il déclaré. Cette visite intervient au terme d’une journée consacrée aux échanges entre la HAC et l’ONC-Niger. Les deux institutions ont notamment convenu de travailler à la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route 2026-2028 de la PRA-UEMOA-Guinée, avec plusieurs priorités liées à la régulation du numérique, à la lutte contre la désinformation et les discours de haine, ainsi qu’à la promotion de l’éducation aux médias et au numérique. Créé en octobre 1997, Guineenews s’est progressivement imposé dans le paysage médiatique guinéen comme un média à l’information sur la Guinée. Cette visite du vice-président de la PRA-UEMOA-Guinée aura ainsi permis de mettre en avant, au-delà des échanges institutionnels, les liens entre les instances de régulation et les médias qu’elles accompagnent.

items.title: Aly Farka Touré, le génie autodidacte
items.description: Sa musique a largement dépassé les frontières de son Mali natal, pour s’imposer, sur les plus grandes scènes internationales. Aly Farka Touré aura toute sa carrière durant défendu l’enracinement du blues, sonorité dont il revendique avec fierté, la paternité africaine. Il y a ceux qui naissent avec des prédispositions naturelles. Il y a ceux qui se façonnent au fil du temps, à force d’apprentissage, de travail et d’abnégation. Et puis, il y a ceux, plus rares, qui réunissent les deux. Ils jouissent d’aptitudes innées auxquelles s’ajoute un désir inlassable d’apprendre, de progresser et de se remettre constamment en question. C’est souvent de cette complémentarité que naît le talent, et parfois même le génie. Aly Farka Touré appartient incontestablement à cette dernière trempe. Virtuose de la guitare, le musicien malien n’a pourtant pas fréquenté les grandes écoles d’art ni suivi les parcours académiques qui façonnent habituellement les grands instrumentistes. Son école à lui est celle de la vie, de la tradition et de l’écoute. Il a puisé dans le patrimoine musical malien pour construire une identité musicale qui allait progressivement dépasser les frontières de son pays et dialoguer avec le blues américain. L’écouter jouer est une expérience qui transcende les règles musicales. Les connaisseurs y reconnaissent la maîtrise d’un guitariste de talent, les profanes, se laissent agréablement emporter par la beauté du son. Aly Farka Touré est né en 1939, dans la région de Tombouctou, au Mali. Dans la publication « Desert Blues / Entre Dunes Et Savanes » qui revient sur le parcours de l'artiste, il est noté «Aly Farka Toure apprend en observant les griots, en s'imprégnant des musiques traditionnelles peules, songhaï, tamasheq et bambara qui circulent le long du fleuve. Sa première guitare, il se la fabrique lui-même, à partir d'une seule corde tendue sur une caisse de résonance artisanale». Cet instrument sonore, ancré dans les répertoires traditionnels, façonne son jeu de guitare électrique. Devant son talent époustouflant et sa maîtrise légendaire des notes, la critique occidentale le surnomme «le John Lee Hooker africain ». Un surnom qui ne l’emballait point, car disait-il, avec fierté, «le blues américain descend des musiques ouest-africaines, et non l'inverse». Une notoriété et des Grammy Award Sa carrière décolle véritablement dans les années 1980, quand il signe un contrat avec le label britannique World Circuit. Sa sonorité transcende tout de suite le Mali. Mais, c'est l'album Talking Timbuktu, enregistré en 1994 avec le guitariste américain Ry Cooder, qui le propulse sur la scène mondiale. Il remporte au passage un Grammy Award. Il en obtiendra un second, à titre posthume, pour « In the Heart of the Moon », enregistré avec le maître de la kora Toumani Diabaté. Cette collaboration scelle symboliquement le dialogue entre deux grandes traditions instrumentales du Mali. Paysan dans l’âme Aly Farka Touré se refusait de faire de la musique une activité à plein temps. Il se définissait avant tout comme agriculteur. Il s'adonne pleinement à l’agriculture et l’élevage. Il fait construire à ses frais une centrale électrique, pour alimenter son village natal. En 2004, il est élu maire de sa ville. Il occupera ce mandat jusqu'à son rappel à Dieu, refusant tout salaire pour cette fonction. Aly Farka Touré s'éteint en mars 2006, peu après avoir achevé l'enregistrement de l’album «Savane», sorti à titre posthume au mois de juillet de la même année. Cet album est salué comme l'un des plus aboutis de son œuvre. Aujourd'hui, sa musique demeure une référence incontournable, pour quiconque s'intéresse aux racines africaines du blues. O.BA

items.title: Washington inclut le Maroc dans un programme de fourniture de composants pour missiles AIM-120
items.description: Le Maroc figure parmi les bénéficiaires d’un nouveau contrat militaire attribué par le département américain de la Défense à l’industriel Raytheon, dans le cadre du programme américain de ventes militaires à l’étranger (Foreign Military Sales, FMS). D’un montant total de 105,6 millions de dollars, l’accord porte sur la fourniture de composants destinés aux missiles air-air de moyenne portée AIM-120 AMRAAM. Selon les informations publiées par le Pentagone, Raytheon s’est vu octroyer un avenant contractuel d’une valeur de 105.646.856 dollars pour la production de composants liés aux « Advanced Medium Range Air-to-Air Missiles » (AMRAAM). Les travaux seront réalisés sur le site industriel de l’entreprise à Tucson, en Arizona, et doivent s’achever le 31 août 2027. Le Royaume apparaît parmi les pays étrangers concernés par le volet du contrat relevant des ventes militaires à l’étranger, aux côtés de plusieurs alliés et partenaires des États-Unis. Le document officiel ne précise toutefois ni le montant réservé au Maroc ni le volume des composants ou équipements qui pourraient être destinés aux Forces armées royales (FAR). Le Pentagone souligne ainsi que les 105,6 millions de dollars annoncés ne correspondent pas à une commande marocaine. Cette enveloppe couvre à la fois des besoins propres aux forces armées américaines et des livraisons destinées à plusieurs pays partenaires dans le cadre du programme FMS. Les documents contractuels indiquent qu’environ 35,65 millions de dollars proviennent des fonds consacrés aux ventes militaires à l’étranger, tandis que le reste du financement est assuré par des crédits américains destinés à l’acquisition de missiles et de composants associés. Aucune répartition détaillée de cette enveloppe entre les pays bénéficiaires n’est cependant fournie, ce qui ne permet pas d’identifier la part revenant au Maroc. Cette nouvelle opération s’inscrit dans la continuité de la coopération militaire entre Rabat et Washington, particulièrement dans le domaine de la modernisation des capacités aériennes marocaines et de l’équipement de la flotte de chasseurs F-16. En décembre 2024, le département américain de la Défense avait déjà annoncé l’approbation, par le département d’État, d’une éventuelle vente au Maroc de jusqu’à 30 missiles AIM-120C-8 AMRAAM, accompagnés d’équipements et de systèmes associés, pour un montant estimé à 88,37 millions de dollars. Cette transaction comprenait également des équipements de test, de maintenance, de soutien logistique, des pièces de rechange et divers matériels nécessaires à leur exploitation. Elle visait à renforcer les capacités des Forces armées royales, notamment celles des F-16 Block 72, au cœur du programme de modernisation des moyens aériens du Royaume. Considéré comme l’un des principaux missiles air-air de moyenne portée en service au sein des forces américaines et de plusieurs armées alliées, l’AIM-120 AMRAAM constitue un élément essentiel de l’armement embarqué sur les F-16 dans de nombreux pays. Au-delà de l’acquisition de nouvelles capacités, l’inclusion du Maroc dans ce contrat illustre également l’importance croissante accordée à la maintenance et au soutien logistique des systèmes d’armes. Les programmes modernes d’armement reposent en effet non seulement sur l’achat de plateformes ou de munitions, mais aussi sur un approvisionnement continu en composants, pièces détachées et services techniques garantissant la disponibilité opérationnelle des équipements. Les documents américains relatifs à la vente des missiles AIM-120C-8 approuvée en 2024 établissaient déjà un lien direct avec la flotte marocaine de F-16 Block 72, indiquant que ces missiles et les équipements associés devaient contribuer au renforcement des capacités opérationnelles des Forces armées royales. Cette nouvelle annonce intervient alors que le Royaume poursuit le développement de ses capacités aériennes à travers l’acquisition et l’équipement de chasseurs F-16, ainsi que le renforcement des dispositifs de maintenance, de soutien et d’armement qui leur sont associés, dans le cadre d’un programme plus large de modernisation de l’aviation militaire marocaine. The post Washington inclut le Maroc dans un programme de fourniture de composants pour missiles AIM-120 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Seychelles : la Russie livre trois tonnes de marchandises sollicitées par Victoria
items.description: La Russie a remis aux Îles Seychelles trois tonnes de marchandises dans le cadre d'un programme humanitaire sollicite par les autorites seychelloises. La ceremonie de remise de l'aide s'est deroulee au port de Victoria le 26 septembre, en presence du vice-president des Seychelles, Sebastien Pillay, et du general de division des forces de defense des Seychelles Michael Rosette. Du cote russe, l'ambassadeur de Russie aux Seychelles, Kirill Sokolov-Chtcherbatchev, et l'amiral Vladimir Vorobiov, commandant en second de la marine russe, etaient presents a l'evenement. Selon ce dernier, la cargaison comprenait des denrees alimentaires, des produits medicaux et des ouvrages sur l'histoire et la culture russes destines a la Bibliotheque nationale des Seychelles. Cette aide a ete acheminee vers l'archipel a bord du navire-ecole Perekop de la flotte de la Baltique de la Marine russe, des eleves des ecoles navales russes effectuant un stage a son bord. Cette visite est deja la deuxieme escale d'un navire de guerre russe aux Seychelles en 2026. Au cours de la ceremonie, Vladimir Vorobiov a declare que, bien que les relations diplomatiques entre les deux pays aient ete etablies en 1976, l'histoire des contacts entre la marine russe et l'archipel remontait a bien plus loin. Il a ajoute que l'arrivee du navire etait consacree a deux dates importantes pour la marine russe : le 330e anniversaire de la Marine russe et le 120e anniversaire des forces sous-marines de la Marine russe. a cette occasion, des expositions ont ete organisees a Victoria, a proximite du navire. Kirill Sokolov-Chtcherbatchev, a quant a lui souligne que la visite du navire constituait une nouvelle confirmation de l'amitie et du partenariat entre Moscou et Victoria. De son cote, le general de division Michael Rosette a declare lors d'un entretien avec le media African Initiative que la cooperation militaro-technique entre la Russie et les Seychelles etait avant tout axee sur la formation des militaires. Selon lui, cette cooperation ne se limitera pas aux escales des navires russes dans le port, mais il est egalement possible qu'un groupe d'instructeurs russes se rende dans l'archipel pour dispenser cette formation. Michael Rosette a ajoute que le format actuel de la cooperation avec la Russie est similaire aux accords que les Seychelles concluent avec d'autres pays. L'arrivee du navire russe dans le port des Seychelles a eu lieu l'annee du 50e anniversaire des relations diplomatiques entre la Russie et les Seychelles. Cet anniversaire coïncidait avec celui de l'independance de l'archipel, qui fete egalement son demi-siecle. Le 29 juin, des ceremonies solennelles, marquees par un defile militaire, ont ete organisees dans le pays pour celebrer ces evenements. La Russie etait representee par le 154e regiment de commandement independant de Preobrajenskiï, une unite qui represente traditionnellement le pays lors des ceremonies importantes a l'etranger. Aux cotes des troupes seychelloises, des detachements venus d'Inde, de Chine et de Maurice ont egalement defile.

items.title: Extractive firms urged to strengthen cyber defences as digital risks grow
items.description: Senior executives from Ghana’s mining, oil and gas industries have discussed the risks that cyberattacks, fraud and emerging technologies pose to their operations at an event hosted by cybersecurity firm e-Crime Bureau. The company held the second edition of its Founder’s Opera Soirée at its East Legon office in Accra on Friday, 25 September 2026. The event, themed “Managing Cyber and Related Risks in the Extractive Sector”, brought industry leaders and professionals together to examine how digital threats could affect safety, business continuity and critical infrastructure. Participants discussed risks arising from the growing links between digital systems, industrial equipment and physical facilities. These included cyberattacks, the misuse of artificial intelligence, insider threats, industrial espionage, supply chain weaknesses and incidents in which a digital breach could have physical consequences. Bridget Otoo addressing the gathering A discussion moderated by Presidential Staffer and media personality Bridget Otoo focused on the protection of data and systems in the extractive sector. It also covered leadership, crisis management, organisational resilience and the need to build cybersecurity expertise. Participants emphasised that managing these risks required coordination across an organisation, from senior management and operational teams to human resources, security staff and external contractors. As mining, oil and gas companies adopt more digital technology, they said, firms must account for the effects a breach could have beyond their computer networks. The event was hosted by e-Crime Bureau’s Founder and Executive Chairman, Dr Albert Antwi-Boasiako. He said the inclusion of Italian opera offered an opportunity for executives to build professional relationships in a setting outside conventional business meetings. Italy’s Ambassador to Ghana and Togo, Laura Ranalli, attended the soirée. According to the organisers, she commended Dr Antwi-Boasiako’s contributions to cybersecurity in Africa and to Ghana-Italy relations. Italy’s Ambassador to Ghana and Togo, Laura Ranalli, at the event on Friday. The event also highlighted opportunities for cooperation in digital transformation, cybersecurity and cultural exchange. Established in 2011, e-Crime Bureau provides cybersecurity consulting, digital forensics, investigations, training and technology services.

items.title: Kano State ranks first in 2026 NECO
items.description: Kano State has ranked first in the 2026 National Examination Council of Nigeria (NECO), with 74,413 candidates that obtained at least five credits, including English Language and Mathematics. The result showed that Lagos emerged second with 72,496 candidates and Oyo came third with 55,543 candidates. The performance marks the second consecutive year that Kano has topped the NECO national performance chart, after recording the highest number of candidates with five credits, including English and Mathematics in the 2025 examination. Reacting to the development, Gov. Abba Yusuf, in a statement by his spokesperson, Mr Sanusi Bature, on Saturday in Kano, commended the students, teachers, parents and other stakeholders for the outstanding performance. Yusuf said the back-to-back performance was an indication that the state’s sustained investment in education was producing measurable results. “Kano has maintained the first position in NECO twice in a row making the state as the leading SSCE performer for the two consecutive years, (2025 and 2026) respectively,” he said He assured the people of Kano that his administration would continue to prioritise education through increased funding, improved learning facilities, teacher recruitment and training, scholarships and support for indigent students. As part of the interventions, he said, the state government spent over N4.4 billion in 2026 to sponsor candidates for Senior Secondary School Certificate Examination, particularly indigent students. The governor said the intervention was designed to remove financial barriers and enable students to participate in the examinations under better conditions. He said the latest NECO result was a continuation of the improvement recorded by Kano students under the present administration. “Education has consistently received the largest share of Kano State’s budget under Governor Yusuf; overshooting the UNESCO benchmark. “In 2024, education accounted for about 29.95 per cent of the state budget. The allocation increased to N168.35 billion, representing 31 per cent, in the 2025 budget. “For 2026, the state allocated N405.35 billion to education, representing about 30 per cent of the N1,478, 829, 666, 130. 71 trillion budget,” he said. The governor said the investment goes beyond examination sponsorship to include classroom renovation, teacher recruitment, learning materials, uniforms, scholarships and other interventions aimed at improving the quality of education. The administration’s education policies have also attracted recognition at national and international levels, with Kano fast becoming a leading education reform hub in sub-Saharan Africa. In 2024, Yusuf received the Leadership Newspaper Governor of the Year Award for Education, while New Telegraph recognised him for educational development Governor of the year. The Nigeria Union of Teachers also named the governor its Teachers’ Friendly Governor of the Year for 2024. “In 2025, Blueprint Newspaper recognised Governor Yusuf as Governor of the Year for Education at the paper’s national conference in Abuja. While This Nigeria newspaper awarded him as courageous Governor of the year 2024. “The administration also received education-related recognition at International space in London and Paris 2026, for its commitment to education with international literacy and learning award and the education spending award by the Universal Learning Solution and City University, Paris respectively,” he said. He said the objective was to build an education system capable of providing Kano’s young people with the knowledge and skills required for higher education, employment, innovation and leadership as Kano has recorded over five million school children in the last annual school census The post Kano State ranks first in 2026 NECO appeared first on Vanguard News .
